```ts
    expect({ ...HEAD_RULES }).toEqual({ tag: "korbat.head.v2", shownDays: 30, witnessTimeoutMs: 10_000, tokenMaxBytes: 16_384 });
    expect([...HEAD_KINDS]).toEqual(["head", "restore"]);
    expect([...HEAD_WITNESSES]).toEqual(["none", "rfc3161", "test"]);
  });

  const VALUE = "917907fc36f065a78e0b730230eac9c4f1c2882c77efc7a868a65ee336e0899e";
  const row = { day: "2026-10-18", kind: "head", value: VALUE, witness: "rfc3161", token: "MAMCAQA=", retiredOn: null, lastDay: null } as const;

  test("PublicHead: a day, its kind, its value, who witnessed it with the token, when a restore retired it and, on a restore, the last day that still fits", () => {
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [row] }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [] }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, witness: "none", token: null }, { ...row, kind: "restore", lastDay: "2026-10-12", retiredOn: null }] }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, retiredOn: "2026-10-19" }] }).success).toBe(true);
    // Never the place, the hash or anything a row does not have.
    for (const extra of [{ chainSeq: 41 }, { seq: 41 }, { hash: VALUE }, { publishedAt: "2026-10-18T07:01:00.000Z" }]) {
      expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, ...extra }] }).success, Object.keys(extra)[0]).toBe(false);
    }
    for (const bad of [{ value: VALUE.toUpperCase() }, { value: VALUE.slice(1) }, { witness: "tsa" }, { kind: "retired" }, { day: "18.10.2026" }, { token: "not base64!" }]) {
      expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, ...bad }] }).success, JSON.stringify(bad)).toBe(false);
    }
    // A token is at most HEAD_RULES.tokenMaxBytes bytes, as base64: four characters for each three bytes.
    const groups = Math.ceil(HEAD_RULES.tokenMaxBytes / 3);
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, token: `${"A".repeat(groups * 4 - 4)}AA==` }] }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(PublicHead.safeParse({ days: [{ ...row, token: "A".repeat(groups * 4 + 4) }] }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

});
```

```ts
      reportAlertHours: 24,
      staleHours: 2,
      quietMinutes: 15,
      escalateMinutes: 15,
      remindMinutes: 45,
      channelDownMinutes: 3,
      pushOwedMinutes: 60,
      copyOverdueHours: 48,
      handoverAlertDays: 7,
      messageKeepDays: 30,
      recordKeepYears: 3,
      gapKeepMonths: 12,
    });
  });

  test("a hold with its one extension ends before the preservation does: hold_days + hold_extension_days days are fewer than preserve_months months", () => {
    // The shortest run of preserve_months calendar months has this many days (February in a common year among them).
    const shortestMonths = 30 * ORDER_RULES.preserveMonths - 3;
    expect(ORDER_RULES.holdDays + ORDER_RULES.holdExtensionDays).toBeLessThan(shortestMonths);
  });

  test("ALERT_RULES holds only what the database never reads, and no name is in both tables", () => {
    expect(ALERT_RULES).toEqual({ pollSeconds: 20, tickSeconds: 30, mailRetryHours: 24 });
    for (const name of Object.keys(ALERT_RULES)) expect(Object.keys(ORDER_RULES), name).not.toContain(name);
  });
});

describe("the contact point's requests and answers", () => {
  const message = {
    id: "3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a",
    folder: "junk",
    receivedAt: "2026-10-12T22:01:02.003Z",
    seenAt: "2026-10-12T22:01:20.000Z",
    stale: false,
    disposition: null,
    handledAt: null,
    handledBy: null,
    orders: [],
  };

  test("ContactPage: messages without a sender or a subject, each strict, at most a page of them", () => {
    expect(ContactPage.parse({ items: [message], nextCursor: null })).toEqual({ items: [message], nextCursor: null });
    expect(ContactPage.safeParse({ items: [{ ...message, subject: "x" }], nextCursor: null }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ContactPage.safeParse({ items: [{ ...message, folder: "spam" }], nextCursor: null }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ContactPage.safeParse({ items: Array.from({ length: CONTACT_PAGE_SIZE + 1 }, () => message), nextCursor: null }).success).toBe(false);
    const handled = { ...message, disposition: "not_an_order", handledAt: "2026-10-12T22:05:00.000Z", handledBy: "mod_anna" };
    expect(ContactPage.parse({ items: [handled], nextCursor: "abc" }).items[0]!.handledBy).toBe("mod_anna");
  });

  test("ContactQuery takes a cursor and open=1 only; ContactCloseRequest a disposition other than order", () => {
    expect(ContactQuery.parse({})).toEqual({});
    expect(ContactQuery.parse({ open: "1", cursor: "abc" })).toEqual({ open: "1", cursor: "abc" });
    expect(ContactQuery.safeParse({ open: "0" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ContactQuery.safeParse({ other: "1" }).success).toBe(false);
    for (const disposition of CONTACT_CLOSE_DISPOSITIONS) expect(ContactCloseRequest.parse({ disposition })).toEqual({ disposition });
    expect(ContactCloseRequest.safeParse({ disposition: "order" }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(ContactCloseRequest.safeParse({ disposition: "referral", note: "x" }).success).toBe(false);
  });

  test("StaffOverview carries the contact point's counts and the channel's state", () => {
    const shape = StaffOverview.shape;
    expect(shape.contact.parse({ open: 2, oldestAt: message.receivedAt, dueAt: message.receivedAt })).toEqual({ open: 2, oldestAt: message.receivedAt, dueAt: message.receivedAt });
    expect(shape.alerts.parse({ channel: "off", since: null })).toEqual({ channel: "off", since: null });
    expect(shape.alerts.safeParse({ channel: "broken", since: null }).success).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("ALERT_TEXTS (W.4): one text serves both legs, and it carries counts and times only (invariant 15)", () => {
  const now = new Date("2026-10-16T09:00:00.000Z");
  /** One set of facts for a kind: every count is `n`, every time the given instant. */
  const factsOf = (kind: AlertKind, n: number, time: string, over: Partial<Record<string, number | string | undefined>> = {}): AlertFacts => {
    const facts: Record<string, number | string> = {};
    for (const name of ALERT_KINDS[kind].facts) facts[name] = isTimeFact(name) ? time : n;
    for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(over)) {
      if (!ALERT_KINDS[kind].facts.includes(name)) continue;
      if (value === undefined) delete facts[name];
      else facts[name] = value;
    }
    return facts;
  };
  const DIGITS = /[0-9]/g;
  const all = (kind: AlertKind, facts: AlertFacts) => {
    const r = renderAlert(kind, facts, now);
    return [r.title, r.sentence, r.todo ?? ""].join(" | ");
  };

  test("rendered with two sets of facts, every kind's title, sentence and line differ only in their digits", () => {
    for (const kind of ALERT_KIND_LIST) {
      // The flags of order_effected and order_opened chose a variant: both sets hold the same flags.
      const flags = { urgent: 0, unknown: 0 };
      // A day (3d's head alerts) prints as its date, so the two sets name two days: they differ in digits alone.
      const first = all(kind, factsOf(kind, 3, "2026-10-16T07:05:00.000Z", { ...flags, day: "2026-10-13T00:00:00.000Z" }));
      const second = all(kind, factsOf(kind, 1234, "2026-10-16T22:49:59.999Z", { ...flags, day: "2026-10-12T00:00:00.000Z" }));
      expect(first.replace(DIGITS, ""), kind).toBe(second.replace(DIGITS, ""));
      expect(first, kind).not.toBe(second);
    }
  });

  test("no entry holds an @, a link or a placeholder that is neither a fact of its kind nor a number of ORDER_RULES, QUARANTINE_RULES, EDGE_WORDS or AUTOMATION_RULES", () => {
    for (const kind of ALERT_KIND_LIST) {
      const text = ALERT_TEXTS[kind];
      const words = [text.title, ...text.sentence.map((part) => part.text), text.todo ?? ""].join(" ");
      expect(words, kind).not.toContain("@");
      expect(words.toLowerCase(), kind).not.toContain("http");
      for (const name of alertPlaceholders(kind)) {
        expect([...ALERT_KINDS[kind].facts, ...Object.keys(ORDER_RULES), ...Object.keys(QUARANTINE_RULES), ...Object.keys(EDGE_WORDS), ...Object.keys(AUTOMATION_RULES)], `${kind}: {${name}}`).toContain(name);
      }
      // Every number a sentence of 3f prints comes from the facts or from ORDER_RULES: no digit is typed. 3c's burst
      // window is 3c's own number, which its push names as its mail does.
      if (ALERT_KINDS[kind].mail !== "own") expect(words.replace(/[{][a-zA-Z]+[}]/g, ""), kind).not.toMatch(DIGITS);
    }
  });

  test("a time prints as 14:05 UTC, with the day when it is not the day of the alert", () => {
    expect(alertTime("2026-10-16T14:05:59.000Z", now)).toBe("14:05 UTC");
    expect(alertTime("2026-10-15T23:59:00.000Z", now)).toBe("2026-10-15 23:59 UTC");
    expect(alertTime("2026-10-17T00:00:00.000Z", now)).toBe("2026-10-17 00:00 UTC");
  });

  test("the words of the kinds Task 1 sends, as W.4 has them", () => {
    const mail = renderAlert("contact_mail", { receivedAt: "2026-10-16T08:05:00.000Z", dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z" }, now);
    expect(mail).toEqual({
      title: "Mail at the contact point",
      sentence: "Mail at the authorities' contact point, received 08:05 UTC. If it is a removal order it is due 09:05 UTC.",
      todo: `Read it in the mail host's app, never in korbat, and with it every other new message there: further mail within ${ORDER_RULES.quietMinutes} minutes raises no alarm of its own. Then open Contact point in the staff console. What ends this message's alarms is handling it there: opening an order from it, or closing it.`,
    });
    // A restart of an order's clock has no time of receipt.
    expect(renderAlert("contact_mail", { dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z" }, now).sentence).toBe("A removal order's hour has started again: due 09:05 UTC.");
    expect(renderAlert("contact_mail_escalated", { receivedAt: "2026-10-16T08:05:00.000Z", dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z" }, now)).toEqual({
      title: "Nobody has answered: mail at the contact point",
      sentence: "Nobody has answered the mail that arrived at the authorities' contact point at 08:05 UTC. If it is a removal order it is due 09:05 UTC.",
      todo: "This went to every staff phone. Whoever reads it first acts, and tells the others.",
    });
    const due = renderAlert("order_due", { dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:05:00.000Z", minutesLeft: 15 }, now);
    expect(due.title).toBe("15 minutes left");
    expect(due.sentence).toBe("A removal order, or mail that may be one, is due 09:05 UTC: 15 minutes are left and it is not carried out in full.");
    expect(due.todo).toBe(
      "Give effect now, to every post the order names. Only if the order has a manifest error, or lacks what you need to find the content, send Annex III and record it: that is no way to stop this alarm. If nobody can act in time: the README, When nobody can act within the hour.",
    );
    expect(renderAlert("mailbox_unreachable", { since: "2026-10-15T23:00:00.000Z" }, now)).toEqual({
      title: "The contact point cannot be read",
      sentence: "korbat has not been able to read the contact-point mailbox since 2026-10-15 23:00 UTC.",
      todo: `Mail that arrives there raises no alert now. Check the mailbox in the mail host's app until this is repaired; an order you find there is opened in the console under Orders, with "The message is not listed". The operator checks the password and the mail host.`,
    });
    expect(renderAlert("alert_channel_down", { since: "2026-10-16T08:57:00.000Z" }, now)).toEqual({
      title: "Phone alerts are down",
      sentence: "Phone alerts are down since 08:57 UTC: korbat's watcher or its push server does not answer.",
      todo: `Until it is repaired, korbat wakes nobody: the mail host's own app on the on-call phone, signed in to the contact-point mailbox and allowed to ring at night, is the only thing that does. Check now that it is. An order you find there is opened in the console under Orders, with "The message is not listed". The operator restarts the notify and ntfy services.`,
    });
    expect(renderAlert("alert_test", { at: "2026-10-16T08:00:00.000Z" }, now)).toEqual({ title: "Daily test", sentence: "Daily test, 08:00 UTC. If you read this on your phone, alerts reach it. Nothing to do.", todo: null });
  });

  test("the pushes of 3c's and 3e's kinds name nobody", () => {
    expect(renderAlert("moderation_urgent", { count: 2, oldestAt: "2026-10-16T08:30:00.000Z" }, now)).toEqual({ title: "Urgent lane", sentence: "2 cases wait in the urgent lane, the oldest since 08:30 UTC.", todo: null });
    expect(renderAlert("moderation_waiting", { count: 4 }, now).sentence).toBe("4 cases or replies are waiting longer than their response time.");
    expect(renderAlert("moderation_burst", { count: 20 }, now).sentence).toBe("One staff account confirmed 20 decisions in 15 minutes. The staff mail says which.");
    expect(renderAlert("moderation_reads", { limit: 200 }, now).sentence).toBe("One staff account opened 200 different cases today. The staff mail says which.");
    expect(renderAlert("moderation_reveal", { at: "2026-10-16T08:59:00.000Z" }, now).sentence).toBe("One staff account revealed who sent a report, at 08:59 UTC. The staff mail says which.");
    expect(renderAlert("moderation_csam_lifted", { at: "2026-10-16T08:59:00.000Z" }, now)).toEqual({
      title: "Reported images are no longer protected",
      sentence: "A decision at 08:59 UTC ended the protection of reported images. Read the staff mail.",
      todo: null,
    });
  });

  test("the variants a fact chooses: an order given effect as urgent, with items still open; the counts of what an order misses", () => {
    expect(renderAlert("order_effected", { items: 3, at: "2026-10-16T08:59:00.000Z", itemsOpen: 0, urgent: 0 }, now).sentence).toBe("An order was given effect at 08:59 UTC: 3 posts disabled.");
    expect(renderAlert("order_effected", { items: 2, at: "2026-10-16T08:59:00.000Z", itemsOpen: 1, urgent: 1 }, now).sentence).toBe(
      "An order that is not verified was given effect as urgent at 08:59 UTC: 2 posts disabled. 1 items of the order are still open.",
    );
    expect(renderAlert("order_opened", { items: 2, dueAt: "2026-10-16T09:30:00.000Z", unknown: 0 }, now).sentence).toBe("An order was opened: 2 items. Due 09:30 UTC.");
    expect(renderAlert("order_opened", { items: 1, unknown: 0 }, now).sentence).toBe("An order was opened: 1 items. No deadline runs.");
    expect(renderAlert("order_opened", { items: 1, unknown: 1 }, now).sentence).toBe("An order was opened: 1 items. Its deadline is unknown: act now.");
    expect(renderAlert("order_unverified", { count: 1, textsMissing: 0, holdsOpen: 2, oldestAt: "2026-10-14T08:00:00.000Z" }, now).sentence).toBe(
      "1 orders are given effect and not verified, or hold a post added after their check, the oldest since 2026-10-14 08:00 UTC. 2 hold a notice with no end recorded.",
    );
    expect(renderAlert("hold_ending", { count: 2, at: "2026-10-20T00:00:00.000Z" }, now).sentence).toBe(`2 held notices are released within ${ORDER_RULES.holdWarningDays} days, the first on 2026-10-20 00:00 UTC.`);
    expect(renderAlert("report_owed", { count: 1, oldestAt: "2026-10-14T08:00:00.000Z" }, now).sentence).toBe(
      `1 reports to the authorities have been owed for more than ${ORDER_RULES.reportAlertHours} hours, the oldest since 2026-10-14 08:00 UTC.`,
    );
  });

  test("a fact that is missing, of another kind, or a string that is no time is refused", () => {
    expect(() => renderAlert("contact_mail_escalated", { receivedAt: "2026-10-16T08:05:00.000Z" }, now)).toThrow(/dueAt/);
    expect(() => renderAlert("moderation_waiting", { count: 1, handle: 7 }, now)).toThrow(/handle/);
    expect(() => renderAlert("alert_test", { at: "mod_anna" }, now)).toThrow(/at/);
    expect(() => renderAlert("moderation_waiting", { count: "4" }, now)).toThrow(/count/);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

  RECIPIENT_RULES,
  TRANSPARENCY_RULES,
  TransparencyFigures,
  band,
} from "../src/index";

/**
 * 3d Task 4, the public figures (design, sections 2 rows 1 to 3 and 8, 6.4, 7.5, 7.6, 10.1 and 10.6): the mirror of
 * transparency_rules() and its band, which a database test holds to the SQL band over 0 to 200; the recipients' rules and
 * the seven signed-out reads they count; and the two public answers, whose schema holds that nothing in them can carry
 * an id, a handle, a day of a decision or a number under ten outside the order section.
 */
describe("the public figures' contracts (3d Task 4)", () => {
  test("TRANSPARENCY_RULES holds transparency_rules()'s five numbers: the floor and the rounding of ten, the due day 1 March, method 1", () => {
    expect({ ...TRANSPARENCY_RULES }).toEqual({ floor: 10, roundTo: 10, dueMonth: 3, dueDay: 1, method: 1 });
  });

  test("band prints 0, 1 to 9, or the count rounded to the nearest ten with halves upward, over 0 to 200", () => {
    for (let n = 0; n <= 200; n++) {
      const expected = n === 0 ? "0" : n < 10 ? "1 to 9" : `about ${Math.floor((n + 5) / 10) * 10}`;
      expect([n, band(n)]).toEqual([n, expected]);
    }
    // LAB E's own rows: 216 is about 220, 14 about 10, 61 about 60, 94 about 90, 35 about 40, 12 about 10.
    expect([216, 14, 61, 94, 35, 12].map(band)).toEqual(["about 220", "about 10", "about 60", "about 90", "about 40", "about 10"]);
    expect([15, 25, 1005].map(band)).toEqual(["about 20", "about 30", "about 1010"]);
    expect(() => band(-1)).toThrow();

  test("no public answer has a member that could hold an id, a handle, a decision's day or a number under ten outside the order section", () => {

    expect(leaves.filter((leaf) => leaf.path.startsWith("head.")).map((leaf) => leaf.path)).toEqual([

      "head.days[].kind",
      "head.days[].value",
      "head.days[].witness",
      "head.days[].token",
      "head.days[].retiredOn",
      "head.days[].lastDay",
    ]);
    const outsideOrders = leaves.filter((leaf) => !leaf.path.includes(".orders"));
    const numbers = outsideOrders.filter((leaf) => leaf.type === "number").map((leaf) => leaf.path);
    expect(numbers.sort()).toEqual(
      [
        "facts.r1.threshold",
        "facts.r1.thresholdVersion",
        "transparency.editions[].method",
        "transparency.editions[].older[].version",
        "transparency.editions[].version",
        "transparency.editions[].year",
      ].sort(),
    );
    const strings = outsideOrders.filter((leaf) => leaf.type === "string").map((leaf) => leaf.path);
    expect(strings.sort()).toEqual(
      [
        "facts.match.dpia",
        "facts.match.dpiaActs",
        "facts.match.source",
        "facts.r1.digest",
        "facts.r1.dpia",
        "facts.r1.dpiaActs",
        "facts.r1.model",
        "facts.r1.publisherClaim",
        "transparency.editions[].older[].publishedOn",
        "transparency.editions[].older[].replacedOn",
        "transparency.editions[].publishedOn",
        // The head (Task 5): a publication's day, its value (a digest that shows neither the place nor a row's hash), the
        // outside token as base64, the day a restore retired it, and on a restore the last day that still fits.
        "head.days[].day",
        "head.days[].value",
        "head.days[].token",
        "head.days[].retiredOn",
        "head.days[].lastDay",
      ].sort(),
    );
    // Every other string leaf is a band, a closed list or a literal.
    expect(outsideOrders.filter((leaf) => leaf.type === "band").length).toBeGreaterThan(10);

/** Collects the leaves of a zod schema with their paths: a band (a string under the band's pattern), an enum, a literal, a string, a number or a boolean. */
function walk(schema: z.ZodType, path: string, out: { path: string; type: string }[]): void {
  const def = (schema as unknown as { def: { type: string } & Record<string, unknown> }).def;
  switch (def.type) {
    case "object":
      for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(def.shape as Record<string, z.ZodType>)) walk(value, `${path}.${key}`, out);
      return;
    case "array":
      walk(def.element as z.ZodType, `${path}[]`, out);
      return;
    case "union":
      for (const option of def.options as z.ZodType[]) walk(option, path, out);
      return;
    case "optional":
    case "nullable":
      walk(def.innerType as z.ZodType, path, out);
      return;
    case "record":
      walk(def.valueType as z.ZodType, `${path}.*`, out);
      return;
    case "string": {
      const checks = (def.checks as { _zod: { def: { check: string; pattern?: RegExp } } }[] | undefined) ?? [];
      const banded = checks.some((check) => check._zod.def.pattern?.source === BAND_SOURCE);
      out.push({ path, type: banded ? "band" : "string" });
      return;
    }
    default:
      out.push({ path, type: def.type });
  }
}

/** The pattern a banded string is held to. */
const BAND_SOURCE = "^(0|1 to 9|about [1-9][0-9]*0)$";
```

```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { actionKind } from "../src/schema/moderation";

/**
 * The rule for the new values of action_kind (3e design, section 6, "The rule for the new enum values"; invariant 1).
 * drizzle's migrator runs every pending migration in one transaction, and a value that ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE added
 * cannot be used as an enum literal before that transaction commits (SQLSTATE 55P04) in anything that is parsed when it
 * is created or run: a view, an SQL-language function, a check, a default, an index predicate, a plain statement. Only a
 * PL/pgSQL body is parsed when it is first called, which no migration statement does. So in 3e's migrations a new value
 * appears as a literal only inside a PL/pgSQL function's body, and everywhere else a kind is compared as text
 * (`kind::text = 'strike'`). This test reads 3e's migration files and refuses any other use.
 *
 * The SQL is read statement by statement, its comments dropped, and every run of white space made one space, so the
 * patterns below need no escapes.
 */

const MIGRATIONS = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "../migrations");

/** 3c's twelve kinds come first in the enum; 3e's ten follow them, and 3f's two follow those (read below). */
const OLD_KINDS = 12;
const KINDS_3E = 10;
const NEW_KINDS: readonly string[] = actionKind.enumValues.slice(OLD_KINDS, OLD_KINDS + KINDS_3E);

/** 3e's first migration: 3c ended at 0019_redaction_scope, so 3e's migrations are 0020 and after. */
const FIRST_3E_MIGRATION = 20;

const NEWLINE = String.fromCharCode(10);
const BREAKPOINT = "--> statement-breakpoint";

/** The journal's entries of 3e's migrations, oldest first. */
function migrationsOf3e(): { idx: number; tag: string }[] {
  const journal = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, "meta", "_journal.json"), "utf8")) as { entries: { idx: number; tag: string }[] };
  return journal.entries.filter((entry) => entry.idx >= FIRST_3E_MIGRATION);
}

/** A statement with its line comments dropped: a comment may name a kind in any words it likes. */
function withoutComments(statement: string): string {
  return statement
    .split(NEWLINE)
    .map((line) => {
      const at = line.indexOf("--");
      return at < 0 ? line : line.slice(0, at);
    })
    .join(NEWLINE);
}

/** Every run of white space (a code point up to the space) as one space, trimmed. */
function flat(text: string): string {
  return [...text]
    .map((char) => (char.charCodeAt(0) <= 32 ? " " : char))
    .join("")
    .split(" ")
    .filter((word) => word !== "")
    .join(" ");
}

/**
 * A statement with the body of a PL/pgSQL function blanked, so that only what is parsed at once is left: a statement that
 * creates a function in LANGUAGE plpgsql keeps its signature and loses what lies between its outer dollar quotes. A DO
 * block keeps its body: it runs inside the migration, and its literals are parsed then.
 */
function withoutPlpgsqlBody(statement: string): string {
  const upper = statement.toUpperCase();
  const creates = upper.startsWith("CREATE FUNCTION") || upper.startsWith("CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION");
  if (!creates || !upper.includes("LANGUAGE PLPGSQL")) return statement;
  const open = statement.indexOf("$$");
  const close = statement.lastIndexOf("$$");
  if (open < 0 || close <= open) return statement;
  return `${statement.slice(0, open + 2)} ${statement.slice(close)}`;
}

/**
 * The places where a literal is compared as text: `::text` followed by `=`, `<>`, `IN (` or `= ANY (ARRAY[` and then a
 * list of quoted words. A new kind's literal there is a text, and parses whatever the enum holds.
 */
const TEXT_COMPARISON = /::text ?(?:=|<>|!=|in ?[(]|= ?any ?[(] ?array ?[[]) ?'[a-z_]+'(?: ?, ?'[a-z_]+')*/gi;

/** The statement that adds a value names it, as a label and not as a literal of the enum. */
const ADDED_VALUE = /alter type [^ ]+ add value '[a-z_]+'/gi;

/** Every use of a new kind's literal in the SQL that is outside a PL/pgSQL body and not compared as text, each with its context. */
function enumLiteralViolations(sqlText: string, kinds: readonly string[] = NEW_KINDS): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  const literal = new RegExp(`'(${kinds.join("|")})'`, "g");
  for (const statement of sqlText.split(BREAKPOINT)) {
    const scanned = withoutPlpgsqlBody(flat(withoutComments(statement)));
    const allowed: [number, number][] = [];
    for (const pattern of [TEXT_COMPARISON, ADDED_VALUE]) {
      for (const match of scanned.matchAll(pattern)) allowed.push([match.index, match.index + match[0].length]);
    }
    for (const match of scanned.matchAll(literal)) {
      const at = match.index;
      const castToText = /^ ?::text(?![a-z_])/i.test(scanned.slice(at + match[0].length));
      if (castToText || allowed.some(([from, to]) => at >= from && at < to)) continue;
      violations.push(scanned.slice(Math.max(0, at - 60), at + match[0].length + 20));
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

describe("the enum-literal rule of 3e's migrations", () => {
  test("action_kind's new values are the ten of 3e, after 3c's twelve", () => {
    expect(NEW_KINDS).toEqual(["strike", "suspend", "terminate", "retire_handle", "warn_reporting", "restrict_reporting", "overrule", "lift_suspension", "unretire_handle", "lift_reporting"]);
  });

  test("3e's migrations are there: the schema (0020) and standing_ledger (0021) at least", () => {
    const tags = migrationsOf3e().map((entry) => entry.tag);
    expect(tags.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(2);
    expect(tags[1]).toBe("0021_standing_ledger");
  });

  test("no file of 3e names a new kind as a literal outside a PL/pgSQL body", () => {
    for (const entry of migrationsOf3e()) {
      const text = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${entry.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
      expect(enumLiteralViolations(text), entry.tag).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  test("the files of 3e do name the new kinds, inside PL/pgSQL bodies, so the test reads what it should", () => {
    const ledger = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${migrationsOf3e()[1]!.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
    // The same file read without blanking the bodies would hold many: the bodies are where the kinds are used.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(ledger.split("LANGUAGE plpgsql").join("LANGUAGE sql")).length).toBeGreaterThan(20);
  });

  test("a deliberate violation of each kind is caught, and the allowed forms are not", () => {
    // Caught: a view, an SQL function, a check and an index predicate that name a new kind as the enum, and a cast.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike';`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE sql AS $$ SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind IN ('suspend', 'terminate')) $$;`)).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`ALTER TABLE decision_actions ADD CONSTRAINT c CHECK (kind <> 'overrule');`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE INDEX i ON decision_actions (created_at) WHERE kind = 'strike';`)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`SELECT 'lift_reporting'::public.action_kind;`)).toHaveLength(1);
    // A DO block runs inside the migration: its body is no exemption.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`DO $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike'; END $$;`)).toHaveLength(1);
    // Two statements: the second's violation is found although the first is a PL/pgSQL function.
    const two = `CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1; END $$;${BREAKPOINT}${NEWLINE}CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'suspend';`;
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(two)).toHaveLength(1);
    // Allowed: a comparison as text, a cast to text, any literal inside a PL/pgSQL body, an old kind, a comment, and the
    // statement that adds the value.
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind::text = 'strike' AND a.kind::text IN ('suspend', 'terminate');`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 'strike'::text AS k;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'strike'; END $$;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`CREATE VIEW v AS SELECT 1 FROM decision_actions a WHERE a.kind = 'remove';`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`-- a.kind = 'strike' in a comment${NEWLINE}SELECT 1;`)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(`ALTER TYPE "public"."action_kind" ADD VALUE 'strike';`)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

/**
 * 3f (design, section 6, "The rule for the new enum values"; invariant 1): the migration orders adds eight values to seven

/** The journal's entries from the migration that adds 3f's values, oldest first. */

    expect(enumLiteralViolations(bodiesToo(text), VALUES_3D)).toEqual([]);

    expect(flat(withoutComments(text))).toContain("i.kind::text = 'automated'");
  });

  test("a deliberate violation is caught even inside a PL/pgSQL body, and the text forms are not", () => {
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(bodiesToo(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1 FROM intakes i WHERE i.kind = 'automated'; END $$;`), VALUES_3D)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(bodiesToo(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1 FROM intakes i WHERE i.channel IN ('system'); END $$;`), VALUES_3D)).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(bodiesToo(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN PERFORM 1 FROM intakes i WHERE i.kind::text = 'automated'; END $$;`), VALUES_3D)).toEqual([]);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(bodiesToo(`CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS jsonb LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$ BEGIN RETURN jsonb_build_object('automated'::text, 1); END $$;`), VALUES_3D)).toEqual([]);
  });
});

/**
 * 3d Task 6 (design, section 6, "The rule for the two new enum values"): the migration automated_decisions adds the two
 * labels, and from it on, as 3e's and 3f's rule says, a label appears as a literal of its enum only inside a PL/pgSQL
 * body, and everywhere else compared or cast as text.
 */
describe("the enum-literal rule of 3d's automated decisions migration", () => {
  const files = (() => {
    const journal = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, "meta", "_journal.json"), "utf8")) as { entries: { idx: number; tag: string }[] };
    const first = journal.entries.find((candidate) => candidate.tag.endsWith("_automated_decisions"));
    return first === undefined ? [] : journal.entries.filter((candidate) => candidate.idx >= first.idx);
  })();

  test("the migration automated_decisions is there, and it adds the two labels", () => {
    // The design numbers it 0035; Tasks 1 to 5 took 0033 to 0037 before it.
    expect(files[0]?.tag).toBe("0038_automated_decisions");
    const text = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${files[0]!.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
    const added = [...flat(text).matchAll(/ALTER TYPE "public"."([a-z_]+)" ADD VALUE '([a-z_]+)'/g)].map((m) => `${m[1]}.${m[2]}`).sort();
    expect(added).toEqual(["intake_channel.system", "intake_kind.automated"]);
  });

  test("no file from it on names either label as a literal outside a PL/pgSQL body", () => {
    for (const entry of files) {
      const text = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${entry.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
      expect(enumLiteralViolations(text, VALUES_3D), entry.tag).toEqual([]);
    }
  });

  test("the file does name the label automated inside decisions_record's body, so the test reads what it should", () => {
    const text = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${files[0]!.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(bodiesToo(text), VALUES_3D).length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4);
  });

  test("3d Task 7: known_material's transparency_figures, replaced, keeps the stricter form: neither label as a literal, in its body either", () => {
    const entry = files.find((candidate) => candidate.tag.endsWith("_known_material"));
    // The design numbers it 0036; Tasks 1 to 6 took 0033 to 0038 before it.
    expect(entry?.tag).toBe("0039_known_material");
    const text = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${entry!.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
    const start = text.indexOf('CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."transparency_figures"');
    const end = text.indexOf("CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION", start + 1);
    expect(start).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    const figures = text.slice(start, end === -1 ? undefined : end);
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(bodiesToo(figures), VALUES_3D)).toEqual([]);
    expect(flat(withoutComments(figures))).toContain("i.kind::text = 'automated'");
  });

  test("3d Task 8: signals_and_retention is read under the stricter form: neither label as a literal, in its bodies either; kinds are compared as text or not at all", () => {
    const entry = files.find((candidate) => candidate.tag.endsWith("_signals_and_retention"));
    // The design numbers it 0037; Tasks 1 to 7 took 0033 to 0039 before it.
    expect(entry?.tag).toBe("0040_signals_and_retention");
    const text = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${entry!.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(bodiesToo(text), VALUES_3D)).toEqual([]);
    // It reads no intake's kind or channel at all: the flag counts signed-in reporters' items by their account alone.
    expect(flat(withoutComments(text))).not.toMatch(/[.](kind|channel)::(intake_kind|intake_channel)/);
    expect(flat(withoutComments(text))).toContain("CREATE FUNCTION");
  });

  test("3d review: 0041_review is read under the stricter form: neither label as a literal, in its bodies either; kinds are compared as text", () => {
    const entry = files.find((candidate) => candidate.tag.endsWith("_review") && candidate.tag.startsWith("0041"));
    expect(entry?.tag).toBe("0041_review");
    const text = readFileSync(path.join(MIGRATIONS, `${entry!.tag}.sql`), "utf8");
    expect(enumLiteralViolations(bodiesToo(text), VALUES_3D)).toEqual([]);
    // Its replaced transparency_figures still compares the intake's kind as text.
    expect(flat(withoutComments(text))).toContain("i.kind::text = 'automated'");
  });
});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

const tables = Object.values(schema).filter((v) => is(v, PgTable)) as PgTable[];
const byName = new Map(tables.map((t) => [getTableConfig(t).name, getTableConfig(t)]));

  test("auth tables live in the auth schema", () => {
    for (const name of ["users", "devices", "sessions", "email_codes", "passkeys", "auth_events"]) {

    }

  });
});

describe("row level security", () => {
  test("every table has RLS enabled and at least one policy", () => {
    expect(tables.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    for (const t of tables) {
      const cfg = getTableConfig(t);
      expect(cfg.enableRLS, cfg.name).toBe(true);
      expect(cfg.policies.length, cfg.name).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });
});

describe("content schema", () => {

  });

    }
  });
});

        "author_notice",
        "author_notice_at",
        "imported_at",
      ].sort(),
    );
    expect(releases.checks.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(["releases_basis", "releases_leave", "releases_notice", "releases_reference", "releases_replay"]);
    // The admin who released is a profile; no foreign key names a seal, a leave or a refusal: a replay may come first.
    expect(releases.foreignKeys.map((fk) => fk.reference().foreignTable[Symbol.for("drizzle:Name") as never])).toEqual(["profiles"]);
    const marks = byName.get("release_posts")!;
    expect(marks.primaryKeys.length + marks.columns.filter((c) => c.primary).length).toBe(1);
    expect(marks.columns.find((c) => c.primary)?.name).toBe("post_id");
    expect(marks.foreignKeys.map((fk) => fk.reference().foreignTable[Symbol.for("drizzle:Name") as never])).toEqual(["releases"]);
    const notices = byName.get("release_notices")!;
    expect(notices.columns.find((c) => c.primary)?.name).toBe("subject_id");
    for (const table of [leaves, releases, marks, notices]) expect(table.enableRLS, table.name).toBe(true);
  });
  test("3d's quarantine_files: a file's row keyed by its image and its name, with its three ends and no right for the API (section 6.1)", () => {
    const files = byName.get("quarantine_files")!;
    expect(files.schema ?? "public").toBe("public");
    expect(files.columns.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(
      ["media_id", "file", "post_id", "size", "sha256", "moved_at", "returned_at", "destroyed_at", "release_id", "lost_at", "lost_told", "imported_at", "unknown"].sort(),
    );
    expect(files.primaryKeys.map((k) => [k.getName(), k.columns.map((c) => c.name)])).toEqual([["quarantine_files_pkey", ["media_id", "file"]]]);
    expect(files.checks.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(["quarantine_files_digest", "quarantine_files_ends", "quarantine_files_file", "quarantine_files_release", "quarantine_files_told"]);
    // Task 2: a destroyed file names the release it was destroyed for.
    expect(files.foreignKeys.map((fk) => fk.reference().foreignTable[Symbol.for("drizzle:Name") as never])).toEqual(["releases"]);
    expect(files.indexes.map((i) => i.config.name).sort()).toEqual(["quarantine_files_post_idx", "quarantine_files_untold_idx"]);
    expect(files.enableRLS).toBe(true);
    expect(files.policies.map((p) => [p.name, p.for, p.to])).toEqual([["quarantine_files_api_none", "select", apiRole]]);
  });
  test("3f's recovery tables: a gap's class and disposition, its closing and the copy marks (section 6.6)", () => {
    const gaps = byName.get("restore_gaps")!;
    expect(gaps.schema ?? "public").toBe("public");
    expect(gaps.columns.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(
      ["id", "import_id", "place", "hash", "action", "target_type", "target_id", "metadata", "acted_at", "imported_at", "class", "closed_at", "closed_by", "disposition"].sort(),
    );
    expect(gaps.checks.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(["restore_gaps_class", "restore_gaps_closed", "restore_gaps_disposition", "restore_gaps_hash", "restore_gaps_place"]);
    expect(gaps.uniqueConstraints.map((u) => u.name)).toEqual(["restore_gaps_place_key"]);
    expect(gaps.indexes.map((i) => i.config.name)).toEqual(["restore_gaps_open_idx"]);
    expect(gaps.enableRLS).toBe(true);
    const marks = byName.get("copy_marks")!;
    expect(marks.columns.map((c) => c.name).sort()).toEqual(["at", "id", "place", "staff_id"]);
    expect(marks.checks.map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(["copy_marks_place"]);
    expect(marks.enableRLS).toBe(true);
  });
  test("the tables 3c retired are gone, with their enums and the reputation column", () => {
    for (const name of ["reports", "strikes", "transparency_log"]) expect(byName.has(name), name).toBe(false);
    for (const name of ["targetType", "reportStatus", "caseAction", "appealStatus", "reports", "strikes", "transparencyLog"]) {
      expect(Object.keys(schema), name).not.toContain(name);
    }
    expect(byName.get("profiles")!.columns.map((c) => c.name)).not.toContain("reputation");
  });
  test("audit_log policies allow only insert and select", () => {
    const kinds = byName.get("audit_log")!.policies.map((p) => p.for).sort();
    expect(kinds).toEqual(["insert", "select"]);
  });
});

describe("account lifecycle 1b", () => {

    const cfg = byName.get("handle_history")!;
    expect(cfg.schema).toBeUndefined(); // public
    // retired_at (3e design, section 6.1): set only by a retirement in the ledger, forced null at insert.
    expect(cfg.columns.map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(["handle_lower", "profile_id", "changed_at", "retired_at"]);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "retired_at")?.notNull).toBe(false);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "retired_at")?.hasDefault).toBe(false);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "handle_lower")?.primary).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "profile_id")?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "changed_at")?.notNull).toBe(true);
    expect(cfg.columns.find((c) => c.name === "changed_at")?.hasDefault).toBe(true);
    const fk = cfg.foreignKeys.map((k) => ({ table: getTableConfig(k.reference().foreignTable).name, columns: k.reference().foreignColumns.map((c) => c.name), onDelete: k.onDelete }));
    expect(fk).toEqual([{ table: "profiles", columns: ["id"], onDelete: "cascade" }]);

  test("profiles record when the handle last changed; users record when their purge finished", () => {

    expect(handleChangedAt).toBeDefined();
    expect(handleChangedAt?.notNull).toBe(false);
    const purgedAt = byName.get("users")!.columns.find((c) => c.name === "purged_at");
    expect(purgedAt).toBeDefined();
    expect(purgedAt?.notNull).toBe(false);
  });
  test("one phone per account: a unique index on phone_hash that leaves out the accounts without one", () => {

    expect(idx?.config.unique).toBe(true);
    expect(idx?.config.columns.map((c) => (c as { name?: string }).name)).toEqual(["phone_hash"]);
    expect(idx?.config.where).toBeDefined();

  test("email codes can be for deleting the account, and every account event of 1b has a type", () => {
    expect(schema.emailCodePurpose.enumValues).toContain("delete_account");

    expect(values.slice(values.indexOf("not_me"), values.indexOf("account_deleted") + 1)).toEqual([
      "not_me",
      "profile_updated",
      "handle_changed",
      "email_changed",
      "badge_verified",
      "badge_removed",
      "export_created",

    ]);
```
