```sql
-- 1. frozen_for, replaced from its text in 0034_release (review H2): the seal arm also holds a released post while its
-- release's notice is held (author_notice 'held'), so until the dispatch round that tells the notice the post reads as it
-- did under the seal: its image rows cannot be deleted, the disposal keeps them, and a decision on its case meets the
-- freeze as before. The other three arms are untouched. It stays an SQL function that names no enum value.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."frozen_for"(post uuid, author uuid) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM public.cases c
      JOIN public.intake_items i ON i.case_id = c.id AND i.suspect AND i.answered_by IS NULL
      WHERE c.closed_at IS NULL AND c.target_type = 'post' AND c.target_id = frozen_for.post)
    OR EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM public.cases c
      JOIN public.intake_items i ON i.case_id = c.id AND i.suspect AND i.answered_by IS NULL
      WHERE c.closed_at IS NULL AND c.target_type = 'account' AND c.target_id = frozen_for.author)
    OR EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM public.seal_posts s
      JOIN public.measures_in_force m ON m.id = s.action_id
      WHERE s.post_id = frozen_for.post
        AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.release_posts r JOIN public.releases x ON x.id = r.release_id
                         WHERE r.post_id = frozen_for.post AND x.author_notice <> 'held'))
    OR public.post_preserved(frozen_for.post)
$$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 2. seal_release, replaced from its text in 0034_release (review M2): after the case's lock and the check that the seal
-- is open, staff_recused when the admin is too close to the seal's case (staff_case_conflict without the reporters, as
-- the routes ask), so a release on a linked account is refused before anything is written and not after its commit.
-- Everything else is 0034's.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."seal_release"(action uuid, basis text, leave uuid, staff uuid) RETURNS uuid
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  a public.decision_actions;
  d public.decisions;
  rules record;
  f record;
  l public.release_leaves;
  v_posts uuid[];
  v_role text;
  v_since timestamptz;
  v_moved timestamptz;
  v_release uuid := gen_random_uuid();
BEGIN
  SELECT x.* INTO a FROM public.decision_actions x WHERE x.id = seal_release.action;
  IF NOT FOUND OR a.kind::text <> 'seal_media' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_not_open';
  END IF;
  SELECT x.* INTO d FROM public.decisions x WHERE x.id = a.decision_id;
  PERFORM 1 FROM public.cases c WHERE c.id = d.case_id FOR UPDATE;
  IF d.kind::text = 'interim' OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.measures_in_force m WHERE m.id = a.id) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_not_open';
  END IF;
  SELECT x.* INTO rules FROM public.release_rules() x;
  SELECT coalesce(array_agg(o.post_id ORDER BY o.post_id), '{}'::uuid[]) INTO v_posts
    FROM (SELECT s.post_id FROM public.seal_posts s
           WHERE s.action_id = a.id AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.release_posts r WHERE r.post_id = s.post_id)
           ORDER BY s.post_id LIMIT rules.posts_max) o;
  IF cardinality(v_posts) = 0 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_not_open';
  END IF;
  -- Review M2: an admin too close to the seal's subject (staff_case_conflict, 3c's recusal) is refused before any fact.
  IF public.staff_case_conflict(seal_release.staff, d.case_id, false) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'staff_recused';
  END IF;

  SELECT x.* INTO f FROM public.release_facts(a.id) x;
  IF NOT f.reported THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_not_reported';
  END IF;
  IF NOT f.quarantined THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_not_quarantined';
  END IF;
  IF f.preserved THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_preserved';
  END IF;

  IF seal_release.basis = 'leave' THEN
    SELECT x.* INTO l FROM public.release_leaves x
     WHERE x.id = seal_release.leave AND x.notification_id = public.seal_record(a.id) AND x.withdrawn_at IS NULL
       FOR SHARE;
    IF NOT FOUND THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_no_leave';
    END IF;
  ELSIF seal_release.basis = 'period' THEN
    IF rules.silence_days IS NULL THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_period_unset';
    END IF;
    v_since := coalesce(f.handed_over_at, (SELECT r.sent_at FROM public.seal_report(a.id) r));
    IF v_since IS NULL OR v_since + make_interval(days => rules.silence_days) > now()
       OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.release_notices n
                       WHERE n.subject_id = a.id AND n.told::text IN ('sent', 'folded')
                         AND n.created_at <= now() - make_interval(days => rules.period_notice_days)
                         AND (n.objection IS NULL OR n.objection_answered_at IS NOT NULL)) THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_period_running';
    END IF;
  ELSE
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_no_leave';
  END IF;

  SELECT u.role::text INTO v_role FROM auth.users u
   WHERE u.id = seal_release.staff AND u.deleted_at IS NULL AND u.role <> 'user' FOR SHARE;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'staff_confirmation_ended';
  END IF;
  IF v_role <> 'admin' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'admin_required';
  END IF;

  SELECT max(q.moved_at) INTO v_moved FROM public.quarantine_files q WHERE q.post_id = ANY (v_posts);
  INSERT INTO public.releases (id, seal_action_id, post_ids, basis, leave_id, their_reference, released_by, released_at, backups_clear_at, author_notice)
  VALUES (v_release, a.id, v_posts, seal_release.basis, l.id, l.reference, seal_release.staff, now(),
          greatest(now(), coalesce(v_moved, now())) + make_interval(days => rules.backup_days), 'pending');
  INSERT INTO public.release_posts (post_id, release_id) SELECT p, v_release FROM unnest(v_posts) AS p;
  UPDATE public.post_media m SET erased_at = now()
    FROM (SELECT x.id FROM public.post_media x WHERE x.post_id = ANY (v_posts) AND x.erased_at IS NULL ORDER BY x.id FOR UPDATE) y
   WHERE m.id = y.id;
  RETURN v_release;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 3. upload_hold_end, replaced from its text in 0039_known_material (review M2 and L4): staff_recused after the admin's
-- check when the admin is too close to the uploader (staff_party_conflict over the uploader alone); and in the end as
-- no_report the uploader's auth.report_holds row is locked FOR UPDATE before the two reads that decide whether the
-- address is released, so a second refusal written meanwhile keeps the hold. Everything else is 0039's.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."upload_hold_end"(refusal uuid, end_as text, reason text, staff uuid) RETURNS void
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  u public.upload_refusals;
  rules record;
  o record;
  v_until timestamptz;
  v_role text;
BEGIN
  SELECT x.* INTO u FROM public.upload_refusals x WHERE x.id = upload_hold_end.refusal FOR UPDATE;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'not_found';
  END IF;
  SELECT m.hold_until INTO v_until FROM public.post_media m WHERE m.id = u.media_id;
  IF NOT (u.end_as IS NULL
          OR (u.end_as = 'report' AND u.release_id IS NULL AND upload_hold_end.end_as = 'no_report')
          OR (u.end_as = 'no_report' AND v_until IS NOT NULL AND v_until > now() AND upload_hold_end.end_as = 'report')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'hold_not_open';
  END IF;
  SELECT x.role::text INTO v_role FROM auth.users x
   WHERE x.id = upload_hold_end.staff AND x.deleted_at IS NULL AND x.role <> 'user' FOR SHARE;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'staff_confirmation_ended';
  END IF;
  IF v_role <> 'admin' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'admin_required';
  END IF;
  -- Review M2: an admin too close to the uploader (3c's recusal, staff_party_conflict) is refused, and nothing is written.
  IF u.owner_id IS NOT NULL AND public.staff_party_conflict(upload_hold_end.staff, ARRAY[u.owner_id], NULL) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'staff_recused';
  END IF;
  IF NOT ((upload_hold_end.end_as = 'report' AND upload_hold_end.reason IS NULL)
          OR (upload_hold_end.end_as = 'no_report' AND upload_hold_end.reason IN ('source_withdrew', 'counsel_no_duty', 'other'))) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_hold_end';
  END IF;

  SELECT x.* INTO rules FROM public.automation_rules() x;
  IF upload_hold_end.end_as = 'no_report' THEN
    UPDATE public.upload_refusals x
       SET ended_at = now(), end_as = 'no_report', end_reason = upload_hold_end.reason, ended_by = upload_hold_end.staff, lifted_told = 'pending'
     WHERE x.id = u.id;
    UPDATE public.post_media m SET hold_until = now() + make_interval(hours => rules.no_report_hours) WHERE m.id = u.media_id;
    -- Review L4: the address's hold row first, FOR UPDATE, as a refusal's trigger takes it: a refusal of the same account
    -- that commits while this waits is then seen by the reads below, each a statement of its own after the lock.
    IF u.owner_id IS NOT NULL THEN
      PERFORM 1 FROM auth.report_holds h WHERE h.user_id = u.owner_id FOR UPDATE;
    END IF;
    IF u.owner_id IS NOT NULL
       AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.authority_notifications n WHERE n.account_id = u.owner_id AND n.state = 'owed')
       AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.upload_refusals x
                        WHERE x.owner_id = u.owner_id AND x.id <> u.id AND (x.end_as IS NULL OR (x.end_as = 'report' AND x.release_id IS NULL))) THEN
      UPDATE auth.report_holds h SET released_at = now(), release_reason = 'declined' WHERE h.user_id = u.owner_id AND h.released_at IS NULL;
    END IF;
  ELSE
    UPDATE public.upload_refusals x
       SET ended_at = now(), end_as = 'report', end_reason = NULL, ended_by = upload_hold_end.staff, lifted_told = NULL
     WHERE x.id = u.id;
    UPDATE public.post_media m SET hold_until = 'infinity'::timestamptz WHERE m.id = u.media_id;
    IF u.end_as = 'no_report' AND u.owner_id IS NOT NULL THEN
      INSERT INTO auth.report_holds (user_id, set_at, seal_final, released_at) VALUES (u.owner_id, u.refused_at, false, NULL)
      ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO NOTHING;
      PERFORM 1 FROM auth.report_holds h WHERE h.user_id = u.owner_id FOR UPDATE;
      UPDATE auth.report_holds h SET set_at = u.refused_at, released_at = NULL, release_reason = NULL
       WHERE h.user_id = u.owner_id AND h.released_at IS NOT NULL;
    END IF;
  END IF;

  UPDATE public.restore_gaps g SET closed_at = now(), closed_by = u.id, disposition = 'reapplied'
   WHERE g.class = 'release' AND g.closed_at IS NULL AND g.action = 'upload_hold_ended' AND g.target_id = u.id::text;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 4. upload_release, replaced from its text in 0039_known_material (review M2): staff_recused right after the refusal's
-- lock when the admin is too close to the uploader. Everything else is 0039's.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."upload_release"(refusal uuid, basis text, leave uuid, staff uuid) RETURNS uuid
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  u public.upload_refusals;
  rules record;
  l public.release_leaves;
  v_role text;
  v_moved timestamptz;
  v_release uuid := gen_random_uuid();
BEGIN
  SELECT x.* INTO u FROM public.upload_refusals x WHERE x.id = upload_release.refusal FOR UPDATE;
  IF NOT FOUND OR u.end_as IS DISTINCT FROM 'report' OR u.release_id IS NOT NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_not_open';
  END IF;
  -- Review M2: an admin too close to the uploader is refused before any fact.
  IF u.owner_id IS NOT NULL AND public.staff_party_conflict(upload_release.staff, ARRAY[u.owner_id], NULL) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'staff_recused';
  END IF;
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.authority_notifications n WHERE n.id = u.notification_id AND n.state = 'sent') THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_not_reported';
  END IF;
  IF (SELECT count(*) FROM public.quarantine_files q WHERE q.media_id = u.media_id AND q.returned_at IS NULL AND q.destroyed_at IS NULL) < 2 THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_not_quarantined';
  END IF;
  SELECT x.* INTO rules FROM public.release_rules() x;
  IF upload_release.basis = 'leave' THEN
    SELECT x.* INTO l FROM public.release_leaves x
     WHERE x.id = upload_release.leave AND x.notification_id = u.notification_id AND x.withdrawn_at IS NULL
       FOR SHARE;
    IF NOT FOUND THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_no_leave';
    END IF;
  ELSIF upload_release.basis = 'period' THEN
    IF rules.silence_days IS NULL THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_period_unset';
    END IF;
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_period_running';
  ELSE
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'release_no_leave';
  END IF;
  SELECT x.role::text INTO v_role FROM auth.users x
   WHERE x.id = upload_release.staff AND x.deleted_at IS NULL AND x.role <> 'user' FOR SHARE;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'staff_confirmation_ended';
  END IF;
  IF v_role <> 'admin' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'admin_required';
  END IF;

  SELECT max(q.moved_at) INTO v_moved FROM public.quarantine_files q WHERE q.media_id = u.media_id;
  INSERT INTO public.releases (id, upload_refusal_id, post_ids, basis, leave_id, their_reference, released_by, released_at, backups_clear_at, author_notice)
  VALUES (v_release, u.id, '{}'::uuid[], upload_release.basis, l.id, l.reference, upload_release.staff, now(),
          greatest(now(), coalesce(v_moved, now())) + make_interval(days => rules.backup_days), 'pending');
  UPDATE public.upload_refusals x SET release_id = v_release WHERE x.id = u.id;
  UPDATE public.post_media m SET erased_at = coalesce(m.erased_at, now()), hold_until = now() WHERE m.id = u.media_id;
  RETURN v_release;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 5. edition_publish, replaced from its text in 0036_transparency (review M3 and M4). M3: before the year's lock, null
-- and nothing written for a year that ended before the oldest account's creation (no profile created before the next
-- year began, which is also the case while no profile exists), so the API never freezes an edition of a year korbat did
-- not run. M4: each version stores in counted_orders the orders transparency_order_ids() named at its instant, and a
-- version hold_ended is due when the list at this call's instant names an order that the newest version's stored list
-- does not (6.4 step 2's "the newest version's orders"), not a list computed again at that version's instant, which
-- reads order_hold_until() as it stands now: an end recorded later with an instant before the version made the order
-- look counted then, and it was left out for good. A version stored before this migration has no list and is read as
-- the list at its instant, as before. The public read never returns the column. Everything else is 0036's.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."edition_publish"(year integer, reason text) RETURNS smallint
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  k record;
  v_at timestamptz;
  v_due timestamptz;
  newest public.transparency_editions;
  v_exists boolean;
  v_version smallint;
  v_reason text;
  v_figures jsonb;
  v_orders jsonb;
BEGIN
  IF edition_publish.reason IS NULL OR edition_publish.reason NOT IN ('first', 'correction') THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_edition';
  END IF;
  IF edition_publish.reason = 'correction' AND session_user <> 'korbat_migrate' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_edition';
  END IF;
  -- Review M3: a year that ended before the oldest account's creation, or any year while no account exists, is no year
  -- korbat ran: nothing is stored for it, whoever asks.
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.profiles p WHERE p.created_at < make_timestamptz(edition_publish.year + 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC')) THEN
    RETURN NULL;
  END IF;
  PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('korbat.edition:' || edition_publish.year::text, 0));
  SELECT * INTO k FROM public.transparency_rules();
  v_at := clock_timestamp();
  v_due := make_timestamptz(edition_publish.year + 1, k.due_month, k.due_day, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC');
  SELECT * INTO newest FROM public.transparency_editions e WHERE e.year = edition_publish.year ORDER BY e.version DESC LIMIT 1;
  v_exists := FOUND;
  IF edition_publish.reason = 'correction' THEN
    IF v_at < v_due THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'edition_not_due';
    END IF;
    IF NOT v_exists THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_edition';
    END IF;
    v_figures := public.transparency_figures(edition_publish.year, v_at);
    v_version := newest.version + 1;
    v_reason := 'correction';
  ELSIF NOT v_exists THEN
    IF v_at < v_due THEN
      RETURN NULL;
    END IF;
    v_figures := public.transparency_figures(edition_publish.year, v_at);
    v_version := 1;
    v_reason := 'first';
  ELSIF EXISTS (SELECT a.id FROM public.transparency_order_ids(edition_publish.year, v_at) AS a(id)
                EXCEPT
                SELECT b.id FROM unnest(coalesce(newest.counted_orders,
                                                 ARRAY(SELECT c.id FROM public.transparency_order_ids(edition_publish.year, newest.computed_at) AS c(id)))) AS b(id)) THEN
    v_orders := public.transparency_orders(edition_publish.year, v_at);
    v_figures := (newest.figures - 'orders') || CASE WHEN v_orders IS NULL THEN '{}'::jsonb ELSE jsonb_build_object('orders', v_orders) END;
    v_version := newest.version + 1;
    v_reason := 'hold_ended';
  ELSE
    RETURN NULL;
  END IF;
  INSERT INTO public.transparency_editions (year, version, computed_at, published_at, method, reason, figures, counted_orders)
  VALUES (edition_publish.year, v_version, v_at, v_at, k.method, v_reason, v_figures,
          ARRAY(SELECT o.id FROM public.transparency_order_ids(edition_publish.year, v_at) AS o(id) ORDER BY o.id));
  -- The system actor (apps/api/src/auth/admin.ts, SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID): no person published it.
  INSERT INTO public.audit_log (actor_id, action, target_type, target_id, metadata)
  VALUES ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', 'edition_published', 'edition', edition_publish.year::text || '.' || v_version::text,
          jsonb_build_object('year', edition_publish.year, 'version', v_version, 'reason', v_reason));
  RETURN v_version;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 6. upload_refusals_logged, SECURITY DEFINER, AFTER INSERT ON upload_refusals (review M7): every refusal writes the
-- system's plain audit row upload_refused on the refusal, naming its image, in the transaction that stored it and as its
-- last write (the trigger's name sorts after upload_refusals_hold's, so it fires after it, and nothing follows a
-- refusal's insert in the media module's transactions). A restore that loses the refusal then loses no fact: the
-- keeper's copy holds the line, and staff.js release-replay holds the upload again (upload_refused_replay).
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."upload_refusals_logged"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  -- The system actor (apps/api/src/auth/admin.ts, SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID): no person refused it.
  INSERT INTO public.audit_log (actor_id, action, target_type, target_id, metadata)
  VALUES ('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000', 'upload_refused', 'upload_refusal', NEW.id::text, jsonb_build_object('mediaId', NEW.media_id));
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."upload_refusals_logged"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "upload_refusals_logged" AFTER INSERT ON "public"."upload_refusals" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."upload_refusals_logged"();--> statement-breakpoint

-- 7. upload_refused_replay(refusal, media): staff.js release-replay for a lost upload_refused line (review M7), as the
-- migrator; EXECUTE to nobody. present, with nothing written, when the restored database holds the refusal, and when the
-- image row is held already or erased (a replay's own mark, so a second run writes nothing). Otherwise the image row
-- `media` names, on no post, is held again: hold_until infinity, so nothing sweeps it and post_media_refused refuses its
-- attach (upload_refused), and it answers held 1; held 0 when no such row is left. A later line of the same upload (its
-- end, its release) is replayed after it, in place order. No gap names a refusal: the line itself is the fact, and the
-- replay takes only lines above the restored head.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."upload_refused_replay"(refusal uuid, media uuid) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  m public.post_media;
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.upload_refusals u WHERE u.id = upload_refused_replay.refusal) THEN
    RETURN 'present';
  END IF;
  SELECT x.* INTO m FROM public.post_media x WHERE x.id = upload_refused_replay.media AND x.post_id IS NULL FOR UPDATE;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RETURN 'held 0';
  END IF;
  IF m.erased_at IS NOT NULL OR m.hold_until = 'infinity'::timestamptz THEN
    RETURN 'present';
  END IF;
  UPDATE public.post_media x SET hold_until = 'infinity'::timestamptz WHERE x.id = m.id;
  RETURN 'held 1';
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."upload_refused_replay"(uuid, uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 8. upload_hold_replay, replaced from its text in 0039_known_material (review M5): the image row is changed only while
-- it is not erased, so the replay of an end as report after the replay of the release erased the row no longer sets its
-- hold to infinity and keeps the file for good. Everything else is 0039's.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."upload_hold_replay"(refusal uuid, media uuid, end_as text, ended_at timestamptz) RETURNS text
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  g public.restore_gaps;
  v_changed integer;
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.upload_refusals u WHERE u.id = upload_hold_replay.refusal) THEN
    RETURN 'present';
  END IF;
  SELECT x.* INTO g FROM public.restore_gaps x
   WHERE x.class = 'release' AND x.closed_at IS NULL AND x.action = 'upload_hold_ended' AND x.target_id = upload_hold_replay.refusal::text
     AND x.metadata ->> 'mediaId' = upload_hold_replay.media::text AND x.metadata -> 'params' ->> 'endAs' = upload_hold_replay.end_as
   ORDER BY x.place, x.id LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'replay_no_gap';
  END IF;
  -- Review M5: a row a replayed release erased already is passed over, so a release replayed before the end never keeps
  -- its file for good.
  IF upload_hold_replay.end_as = 'report' THEN
    UPDATE public.post_media m SET hold_until = 'infinity'::timestamptz WHERE m.id = upload_hold_replay.media AND m.post_id IS NULL AND m.erased_at IS NULL;
  ELSE
    UPDATE public.post_media m SET erased_at = now(), hold_until = now() WHERE m.id = upload_hold_replay.media AND m.post_id IS NULL AND m.erased_at IS NULL;
  END IF;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_changed = ROW_COUNT;
  UPDATE public.restore_gaps x SET closed_at = now(), disposition = 'imported' WHERE x.id = g.id;
  RETURN format('replayed %s', v_changed);
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 9. The keeper's mail on the day's head row (review M13): the API's role may set keeper_mailed_at, the column the
-- generated lines above add, once, from null, at the clock's time. head_publications_insert and head_publications_guard
-- are replaced from their texts in 0037_head_publications with that column and nothing else: an insert by any role but
-- the migrator leaves it null, and the guard lets it change only from null, forcing now().
GRANT UPDATE ("keeper_mailed_at") ON "public"."head_publications" TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
-- A value published before this migration was mailed, if at all, by the round that published it, which kept no state:
-- it is taken as mailed, so the first day after the upgrade raises no head_unmailed for it.
UPDATE "public"."head_publications" SET "keeper_mailed_at" = "published_at" WHERE "kind" = 'head' AND "published_at" IS NOT NULL;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."head_publications_insert"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  v_seq bigint;
  v_hash text;
BEGIN
  IF current_user = 'korbat_migrate' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  SELECT a.seq, a.hash INTO v_seq, v_hash FROM public.audit_head a WHERE a.id = 1;
  NEW.kind := 'head';
  NEW.day := (now() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date;
  NEW.chain_seq := v_seq;
  NEW.value := public.head_value(NEW.day, v_seq, v_hash);
  NEW.token := NULL;
  NEW.witnessed_at := NULL;
  NEW.published_at := NULL;
  NEW.retired_at := NULL;
  NEW.last_day := NULL;
  NEW.keeper_mailed_at := NULL;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."head_publications_guard"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF current_user = 'korbat_migrate' THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;
  IF NEW.day IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.day OR NEW.kind IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.kind OR NEW.chain_seq IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.chain_seq
     OR NEW.value IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.value OR NEW.witness IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.witness OR NEW.retired_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.retired_at
     OR NEW.last_day IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.last_day
     OR (OLD.token IS NOT NULL AND NEW.token IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.token)
     OR (OLD.witnessed_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.witnessed_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.witnessed_at)
     OR (OLD.published_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.published_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.published_at)
     OR (OLD.keeper_mailed_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.keeper_mailed_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.keeper_mailed_at) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'moderation_column' USING ERRCODE = '42501';
  END IF;
  IF OLD.witnessed_at IS NULL AND NEW.witnessed_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.witnessed_at := now();
  END IF;
  IF OLD.published_at IS NULL AND NEW.published_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.published_at := now();
  END IF;
  IF OLD.keeper_mailed_at IS NULL AND NEW.keeper_mailed_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.keeper_mailed_at := now();
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 10. quarantine_files_update, replaced from its text in 0033_quarantine (review M12): a lost file's notice may move from
-- none to pending, and then only to what quarantine_lost_told() says at that moment; every other change of lost_told is
-- still from pending alone. Everything else is 0033's.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."quarantine_files_update"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  NEW.media_id := OLD.media_id;
  NEW.file := OLD.file;
  NEW.post_id := OLD.post_id;
  NEW.unknown := OLD.unknown;
  NEW.imported_at := OLD.imported_at;
  IF OLD.sha256 IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.size := OLD.size;
    NEW.sha256 := OLD.sha256;
  END IF;
  IF OLD.returned_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.returned_at IS NULL THEN
    NEW.moved_at := now();
  END IF;
  IF OLD.returned_at IS NULL AND NEW.returned_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.returned_at := now();
  END IF;
  IF OLD.destroyed_at IS NULL AND NEW.destroyed_at IS NOT NULL THEN
    NEW.destroyed_at := now();
  END IF;
  IF NEW.lost_at IS NULL THEN
    NEW.lost_told := NULL;
  ELSIF OLD.lost_at IS NULL THEN
    NEW.lost_at := now();
    NEW.lost_told := public.quarantine_lost_told(NEW.media_id);
  ELSIF OLD.lost_told::text = 'none' AND NEW.lost_told::text = 'pending' THEN
    -- Review M12: a notice owed to nobody when the file was lost (its image sealed for good) is weighed again when the
    -- seal ends: owed (pending) only for an image of a post its author still has, not erased and not sealed for good.
    NEW.lost_told := public.quarantine_lost_told(NEW.media_id);
  ELSIF OLD.lost_told::text <> 'pending' OR NEW.lost_told IS NULL THEN
    NEW.lost_told := OLD.lost_told;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 11. post_media_lost_told, SECURITY DEFINER, AFTER UPDATE OF moderation_state ON post_media (review M12): when an image
-- stops being sealed (the seal for good that was in force over its post is lifted), its lost files' notices that were
-- owed to nobody while it was sealed are weighed again, so lost_untold() lists the image and the dispatch round mails its
-- author image_lost once. A file lost while the image was sealed for good was born with lost_told none, and nothing else
-- changes that.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."post_media_lost_told"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF OLD.moderation_state::text = 'sealed' AND NEW.moderation_state::text <> 'sealed' THEN
    UPDATE public.quarantine_files q SET lost_told = 'pending'
     WHERE q.media_id = NEW.id AND q.lost_at IS NOT NULL AND q.lost_told::text = 'none';
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."post_media_lost_told"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "post_media_lost_told" AFTER UPDATE OF "moderation_state" ON "public"."post_media" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "public"."post_media_lost_told"();--> statement-breakpoint

-- 12. transparency_figures, replaced from its text in 0039_known_material (review L5): the uploads' table reads each
-- refusal's end as it stood on the due day from the newest upload_hold_ended audit row before that day, so a correction
-- computed later prints the same fates as the version of the due day. It keeps its JSON keys, compares the intake kinds as
-- text and reads clock_timestamp(), as 0036 and 0039 wrote it. Everything else is 0039's.
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION "public"."transparency_figures"(year integer, as_of timestamptz) RETURNS jsonb
LANGUAGE plpgsql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  k record;
  v_from timestamptz := make_timestamptz(transparency_figures.year, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC');
  v_to timestamptz := make_timestamptz(transparency_figures.year + 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC');
  v_due timestamptz;
  v_figures jsonb;
  v_orders jsonb;
  v_r1 record;
  v_months record;
BEGIN
  SELECT * INTO k FROM public.transparency_rules();
  v_due := make_timestamptz(transparency_figures.year + 1, k.due_month, k.due_day, 0, 0, 0, 'UTC');
  IF transparency_figures.as_of IS NULL OR transparency_figures.as_of < v_due OR clock_timestamp() < v_due THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'edition_not_due';
  END IF;

  v_figures := jsonb_build_object(
    'restrictions', jsonb_build_object(
      'byGround', public.transparency_fold((
        SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('label', g.label, 'n', g.n) ORDER BY g.label = 'law', g.label)
          FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN d.ground::text = 'illegal' THEN 'law' ELSE d.rule_id END AS label, count(*) AS n
                  FROM public.decisions d
                 WHERE d.kind::text IN ('interim', 'final') AND d.outcome::text = 'restricted' AND d.decided_at >= v_from AND d.decided_at < v_to
                 GROUP BY 1) g)),
      'byMeasure', public.transparency_fold((
        SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('label', g.label, 'n', g.n) ORDER BY g.label)
          FROM (SELECT a.kind::text AS label, count(*) AS n
                  FROM public.decision_actions a JOIN public.decisions d ON d.id = a.decision_id
                 WHERE d.kind::text IN ('interim', 'final') AND d.outcome::text = 'restricted' AND d.decided_at >= v_from AND d.decided_at < v_to
                   AND a.reverses_action_id IS NULL
                 GROUP BY 1) g)),
      'total', public.band((
        SELECT count(*) FROM public.decisions d
         WHERE d.kind::text IN ('interim', 'final') AND d.outcome::text = 'restricted' AND d.decided_at >= v_from AND d.decided_at < v_to))),
    'noBreach', public.band((
      SELECT count(*) FROM public.decisions d
       WHERE d.kind::text = 'final' AND d.outcome::text IN ('no_violation', 'not_evident') AND d.decided_at >= v_from AND d.decided_at < v_to)),
    'intakes', public.transparency_fold((
      SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('label', g.label, 'n', g.n) ORDER BY array_position(ARRAY['rules', 'illegal', 'finding', 'automated'::text], g.label))
        FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN i.kind::text = 'user' THEN CASE WHEN i.alleges_illegal THEN 'illegal' ELSE 'rules' END ELSE i.kind::text END AS label, count(*) AS n
                FROM public.intakes i
               WHERE i.kind::text <> 'order' AND i.received_at >= v_from AND i.received_at < v_to
               GROUP BY 1) g)),
    'appeals', public.transparency_fold((
      SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('label', g.label, 'n', g.n) ORDER BY array_position(ARRAY['kept', 'partly_reversed', 'reversed'], g.label))
        FROM (SELECT a.result::text AS label, count(*) AS n
                FROM public.appeals a JOIN public.decisions r ON r.id = a.answered_by
               WHERE a.result IS NOT NULL AND r.decided_at >= v_from AND r.decided_at < v_to
               GROUP BY 1) g)),
    'reexaminations', public.transparency_fold((
      SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('label', g.label, 'n', g.n) ORDER BY g.label)
        FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN x.outcome::text IN ('restricted_rule', 'restricted_legal', 'partly_reversed', 'reversed') THEN 'action' ELSE 'no_action' END AS label, count(*) AS n
                FROM public.intake_items x JOIN public.decisions r ON r.id = x.answered_by
               WHERE x.reexamines_item_id IS NOT NULL AND r.kind::text <> 'order' AND r.decided_at >= v_from AND r.decided_at < v_to
               GROUP BY 1) g)),
    'accountMeasures', public.transparency_fold((
      SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('label', g.label, 'n', g.n)
                       ORDER BY array_position(ARRAY['strike', 'suspend', 'terminate', 'retire_handle', 'warn_reporting', 'restrict_reporting'], g.label))
        FROM (SELECT a.kind::text AS label, count(*) AS n
                FROM public.decision_actions a JOIN public.decisions d ON d.id = a.decision_id
               WHERE a.kind::text IN ('strike', 'suspend', 'terminate', 'retire_handle', 'warn_reporting', 'restrict_reporting')
                 AND d.kind::text <> 'order' AND d.decided_at >= v_from AND d.decided_at < v_to
               GROUP BY 1) g)),
    'automated'::text, jsonb_build_object(
      'findings', public.transparency_fold((
        SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('label', g.label, 'n', g.n) ORDER BY g.label)
          FROM (SELECT i.rule_id AS label, count(*) AS n
                  FROM public.intakes i
                 WHERE i.kind::text = 'automated' AND i.rule_id IS NOT NULL AND i.received_at >= v_from AND i.received_at < v_to
                 GROUP BY 1) g)),
      'measures', public.transparency_fold((
        SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('label', g.label, 'n', g.n) ORDER BY g.label)
          FROM (SELECT d.rule_id AS label, count(*) AS n
                  FROM public.decisions d
                 WHERE d.decided_by IS NULL AND d.kind::text IN ('interim', 'final') AND d.outcome::text = 'restricted' AND d.rule_id IS NOT NULL
                   AND d.decided_at >= v_from AND d.decided_at < v_to
                 GROUP BY 1) g))));

  -- The programs' rate (section 2, row 23): of the year's findings by a program under R1, those whose case a person's
  -- final decision had restricted by the due day; printed only as two bands, and only on a base of ten or more.
  SELECT count(*) AS base,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.intake_items t JOIN public.decisions f ON f.case_id = t.case_id
                                         WHERE t.intake_id = i.id AND f.kind::text = 'final' AND f.outcome::text = 'restricted'
                                           AND f.decided_by IS NOT NULL AND f.decided_at < v_due)) AS restricted
    INTO v_r1
    FROM public.intakes i
   WHERE i.kind::text = 'automated' AND i.rule_id = 'R1' AND i.received_at >= v_from AND i.received_at < v_to;
  IF v_r1.base >= k.floor THEN
    v_figures := jsonb_set(v_figures, '{automated,r1}', jsonb_build_object('base', public.band(v_r1.base), 'restricted', public.band(v_r1.restricted)));
  END IF;

  -- 0039 (6.4's row of uploads): the year's refusals by refused_at, by how their hold had ended by the due day (report,
  -- no_report) or that it had not (open). A row is folded and banded as every table is. Review L5: the end as it stood on
  -- the due day is the newest upload_hold_ended audit row of the refusal before that day, since an end changed after it
  -- (report to no_report or back) moves ended_at past it; a refusal without such a row reads its columns, as before.
  v_figures := v_figures || jsonb_build_object('uploads', public.transparency_fold((
    SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('label', g.label, 'n', g.n) ORDER BY array_position(ARRAY['report', 'no_report', 'open'], g.label))
      FROM (SELECT coalesce((SELECT a.metadata -> 'params' ->> 'endAs' FROM public.audit_log a
                              WHERE a.action = 'upload_hold_ended' AND a.target_type = 'upload_refusal' AND a.target_id = u.id::text
                                AND a.created_at < v_due
                              ORDER BY a.chain_seq DESC LIMIT 1),
                            CASE WHEN u.ended_at IS NOT NULL AND u.ended_at < v_due THEN u.end_as ELSE 'open' END) AS label, count(*) AS n
              FROM public.upload_refusals u
             WHERE u.refused_at >= v_from AND u.refused_at < v_to
             GROUP BY 1) g)));

  v_orders := public.transparency_orders(transparency_figures.year, transparency_figures.as_of);
  IF v_orders IS NOT NULL THEN
    v_figures := v_figures || jsonb_build_object('orders', v_orders);
  END IF;

  -- The six full months before the due day, the same in every version of the year, whatever as_of is.
  SELECT count(*) AS months, avg(m.signed_in) AS signed_in, avg(m.signed_out_days) AS signed_out, bool_and(m.signed_out_days IS NOT NULL) AS counted_out
    INTO v_months
    FROM public.recipient_months m
   WHERE m.month >= (date_trunc('month', v_due AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') - make_interval(months => 6))::date
     AND m.month < date_trunc('month', v_due AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date;
  v_figures := v_figures || jsonb_build_object('recipients',
    CASE WHEN v_months.months < 6 THEN to_jsonb('not recorded'::text)
         WHEN v_months.counted_out THEN jsonb_build_object('low', public.band(round(v_months.signed_in)::bigint),
                                                           'high', public.band(round(v_months.signed_in + v_months.signed_out)::bigint))
         ELSE jsonb_build_object('low', public.band(round(v_months.signed_in)::bigint)) END);
  RETURN v_figures;
END $$;
```

### Create `packages/db/migrations/meta/0041_snapshot.json`

```json
{
  "id": "1ce12a62-b8ed-4f5a-9213-3c3288158d1a",

        }
      },
      "checkConstraints": {
        "decisions_rule_id": {
          "name": "decisions_rule_id",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2', 'R3', 'R4', 'R5', 'R6')"
        },
        "decisions_category": {
          "name": "decisions_category",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category\" in ('STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE')"
        },
        "decisions_category_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_category_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" in ('KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT')"
        },
        "decisions_automated_decision": {
          "name": "decisions_automated_decision",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"automated_decision\" in ('fully', 'partially', 'not_automated')"
        },
        "decisions_territorial_scope": {
          "name": "decisions_territorial_scope",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"territorial_scope\" = 'worldwide'"
        },
        "decisions_review_target": {
          "name": "decisions_review_target",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"kind\" in ('review', 'correction')) = (\"decisions\".\"reviews_decision_id\" is not null) and (\"decisions\".\"kind\" = 'review') = (\"decisions\".\"appeal_id\" is not null)"
        },
        "decisions_interim": {
          "name": "decisions_interim",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" <> 'interim' or \"decisions\".\"through_seq\" = 0"
        },
        "decisions_ground_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'incompatible' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is not null"
        },
        "decisions_ground_law": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_law",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'order'"
        },
        "decisions_restricted": {
          "name": "decisions_restricted",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"outcome\" <> 'restricted' or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is not null and ((\"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is not null and \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is not null) or \"decisions\".\"decided_by\" is null)) or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'order'"
        },
        "decisions_decider": {
          "name": "decisions_decider",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"decided_by\" is null) = (\"decisions\".\"automated_decision\" = 'fully') and (\"decisions\".\"decided_by\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'interim')"
        },
        "decisions_match_answer_reason": {
          "name": "decisions_match_answer_reason",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"match_answer_reason\" in ('source_withdrew', 'counsel', 'other')"
        },
        "decisions_informed": {
          "name": "decisions_informed",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"informed_at\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"author_mail\"::text = 'none'"
        },
        "decisions_digests": {
          "name": "decisions_digests",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$')"
        },
        "decisions_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null or \"decisions\".\"ground\" is not distinct from 'illegal'"
        },
        "decisions_law_no_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_law_no_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null"
        },
        "decisions_reversal_plain": {
          "name": "decisions_reversal_plain",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" not in ('review', 'correction') or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is null and \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null and \"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null and \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null and \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null)"
        }
      },
      "isRLSEnabled": true
    },

      "checkConstraints": {
        "intakes_ref": {
          "name": "intakes_ref",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"ref\" ~ '^N-[A-Z2-7]{10}$'"
        },
        "intakes_rule_id": {
          "name": "intakes_rule_id",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2', 'R3', 'R4', 'R5', 'R6')"
        },
        "intakes_category": {
          "name": "intakes_category",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"category\" in ('STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE')"
        },
        "intakes_category_keyword": {
          "name": "intakes_category_keyword",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"category_keyword\" in ('KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL', 'KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL_DEEPFAKE', 'KEYWORD_GROOMING_SEXUAL_ENTICEMENT_MINORS')"
        },
        "intakes_cited_law_len": {
          "name": "intakes_cited_law_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"intakes\".\"cited_law\") <= 300"
        },
        "intakes_explanation_len": {
          "name": "intakes_explanation_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"intakes\".\"explanation\") <= 2000"
        },
        "intakes_has_ground": {
          "name": "intakes_has_ground",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is not null or \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"csam\" or \"intakes\".\"kind\"::text = 'automated'"
        },
        "intakes_illegal_elements": {
          "name": "intakes_illegal_elements",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\" <> 'user' or not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"csam\" or (\"intakes\".\"bona_fide\" and (\"intakes\".\"explanation\" is not null or \"intakes\".\"erased_at\" is not null))"
        },
        "intakes_finding_legal": {
          "name": "intakes_finding_legal",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\" <> 'finding' or not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\""
        },
        "intakes_illegal_not_tc": {
          "name": "intakes_illegal_not_tc",
          "value": "not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"category\" <> 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC'"
        },
        "intakes_csam": {
          "name": "intakes_csam",
          "value": "not \"intakes\".\"csam\" or (\"intakes\".\"category\" = 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS' and \"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null and \"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null)"
        },
        "intakes_contact_signed_out": {
          "name": "intakes_contact_signed_out",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_out'"
        },
        "intakes_reporter_signed_in": {
          "name": "intakes_reporter_signed_in",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_in'"
        },
        "intakes_finding": {
          "name": "intakes_finding",
          "value": "(\"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding') = (\"intakes\".\"finding_by\" is not null) and (\"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding') = (\"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'staff') and (\"intakes\".\"kind\"::text = 'automated') = (\"intakes\".\"channel\"::text = 'system')"
        },
        "intakes_lookup": {
          "name": "intakes_lookup",
          "value": "(\"intakes\".\"lookup_hash\" is not null) = (\"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_out' or \"intakes\".\"csam\")"
        },
        "intakes_erased": {
          "name": "intakes_erased",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"erased_at\" is null or (\"intakes\".\"explanation\" is null and \"intakes\".\"cited_law\" is null)"
        },
        "intakes_r2_finding_only": {
          "name": "intakes_r2_finding_only",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is distinct from 'R2' or \"intakes\".\"kind\"::text in ('finding', 'automated')"
        },
        "intakes_automated": {
          "name": "intakes_automated",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\"::text <> 'automated' or (\"intakes\".\"automated_processing\" and (\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2')) and not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" and not \"intakes\".\"csam\" and \"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null and \"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null and \"intakes\".\"finding_by\" is null)"
        }
      },
      "isRLSEnabled": true
    },

        },
```

### Replace `README.md` (whole file)

````markdown
# korbat

Pseudonymous social platform with a narrow public rulebook and transparent moderation. Self-hosted.

- Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-korbat-design.md`
- Accounts and sessions (sub-project 1a): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-identity-auth-1a-design.md`
- Posting and feed (sub-project 2a): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-posting-feed-2a-design.md`
- Plans: `docs/superpowers/plans/`

## Dev quick start
```bash
pnpm install
node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs                # creates or completes infra/.env, apps/api/.env, apps/app/.env and apps/worker/.env, and derives apps/api/.env.test; values are random and never printed
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml up -d postgres redis counts mailpit   # dev host ports 55432, 56379, 56380, 51025, 58025 (movable: DEV_*_PORT in infra/.env)
pnpm --filter @korbat/api dev               # http://localhost:3000/api/health; reads apps/api/.env
pnpm --filter @korbat/worker dev            # the image worker; reads apps/worker/.env and works on .data/media
pnpm --filter @korbat/app web               # http://localhost:8081
pnpm --filter @korbat/admin dev             # the staff console at http://localhost:8090 (never 127.0.0.1); forwards /api/staff/* to the API above
```

Emails sent in development (sign-in codes, new-device alerts, lockout notices) land in Mailpit at http://localhost:58025. Locally the web app uses Cloudflare's always-pass Turnstile test key, so the human check never blocks you.

The data services are PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey (the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, still under the service name `redis`, on its own volume `valkeydata`: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into the old `redisdata` volume, which held only transient state and can be removed with `docker volume rm`). Valkey needs the password from `infra/.env`; `gen-dev-env` writes it into the API's `REDIS_URL` too, so an older `.env` is fixed by running it again. The recipients' count (the day's key and the counting sketches of the transparency page) lives in a Valkey of its own, the service `counts`, which writes nothing to disk: no append-only file, no snapshot, no volume. A restart of `counts` loses the running month's count, which then reads "not recorded"; nothing else is kept there. It takes the same password, and the API reads it as `COUNTS_URL`, which Compose sets.

korbat once ran MinIO and never used it. Images live on two Docker volumes instead, `media-uploads` and `media-store`. If an old stack left a `korbat_miniodata` volume behind, `docker volume rm korbat_miniodata` removes it.

## Tests
```bash
pnpm test                                     # unit tests of every package
node scripts/test-db.mjs                      # creates or migrates the korbat_test database; run it again after adding a migration
pnpm --filter @korbat/api test:integration    # needs postgres, redis and mailpit up
```

Integration tests have their own database, `korbat_test`, and their own Redis database, 15. Both are named in `apps/api/.env.test`, which `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` derives from `apps/api/.env`. Every run starts by emptying them, and refuses to start if a URL points anywhere else, so tests never touch development data.

Before they had their own database, the integration suites left accounts, profiles and posts in the development database, and the smoke test still leaves its first account per run, by then a moderator, with one open moderation case on that account's post. To see and remove them:

```bash
node scripts/clean-dev-fixtures.mjs          # lists test accounts and profiles without an account; deletes nothing
node scripts/clean-dev-fixtures.mjs --yes    # deletes them with everything they made
```

It only matches emails of the tests' shape, `<word>-<uuid>@korbat.local`, recomputes the counters of kept profiles and posts they touched, and refuses to run unless `API_APP_ORIGIN` in `infra/.env` is a localhost origin. It keeps an account that holds a staff key or that the moderation record names (one that decided anything, one on either side of a staff link, the subject of a case that a decision or a reveal names), and counts it as kept; every other case about a deleted account or one of its posts is deleted with it, the smoke test's open case included.

## Full stack
```bash
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml up -d --build   # http://localhost:8080, and the staff console at http://localhost:8090
node scripts/smoke-auth-stack.mjs --base http://localhost:8080 --console http://localhost:8090 --mailpit http://localhost:58025 --terms draft-2026-09 -- docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml
```

The smoke test first checks the staff console's site: its page carries the console's own policy and is never stored, and the staff API answers there (401 without a session) and nowhere else (Caddy's own 404 on the app's site); the console's case routes (the overview, the queue, a case, the appeals) answer the same two ways, and the console's site refuses the app's own moderation routes with a 404 of its own. It then signs up a throwaway account through Caddy, reads its code from Mailpit, posts and reads the post back from the public Latest timeline. It uploads a JPEG carrying a GPS position, posts it, and checks that the served file is a fresh WebP without metadata, that a symlink planted in the store from inside the worker gets a 404, and that deleting the post removes the image from disk. It checks the worker's isolation, then grants the account a staff role with the CLI and checks that its session was revoked. A second throwaway account edits its bio, changes its handle, reports the first account's post under a rule, finds that report undecided in its own list and as the last member, `moderation`, of its export, and deletes itself. Last, signed out, a notice that the same post is illegal is taken with the human check: it answers a reference and a token, the status page opens with that token, the receipt arrives in Mailpit, and the token in the receipt's link opens the same page. Nothing in it decides the case, since a decision needs a staff key: every run leaves one open case in lane 2 on the first account's post. One network can run it five times an hour and twenty times a day, since its two sign-ups count against the hourly sign-up limit and its signed-out notice against the limits of reports sent without an account.

After every sharp upgrade, add `--worst-case`: it also uploads flat-colour files at the pixel caps (48 MP 16-bit interlaced PNG, 48 MP progressive JPEG, 48 MP GIF, 16 MP AVIF), expects each to be ready without the worker being OOM-killed or restarted, and prints the worker's memory peak.

Caddy listens on 8080 inside its container as its own user, proxies `/api` to the API and serves the web app with the page's security headers; `index.html` is revalidated on every load and the hashed bundles are cached for a year. On 8090 it serves the staff console under the console's own policy and proxies only `/api/staff/*`, which the app's site refuses. On 8091 it serves the phones' push site: only the two alert topics' subscriptions reach ntfy, and every other path is Caddy's own 404. The compose file keeps cloudflared, Caddy, the API and the data services on separate networks, so cloudflared reaches only Caddy and Caddy only the API and ntfy. Under the Compose profile `notify`, the contact point's watcher (`notify`) and the push server (ntfy) join two networks of their own: `push`, which has no route out and whose clients the app's and the console's sites refuse with 403, and `watch`, which holds the watcher and PostgreSQL and nothing else. With the profile on, add `--push http://localhost:8091` to the smoke test: it checks that the push site answers ntfy's own API with 404 and hands a subscription to ntfy, and that from the push network the app's and the console's sites answer 403.

## Upgrading PostgreSQL

The stack runs PostgreSQL 18 on the `pgdata18` volume. A database from the earlier PostgreSQL 16 volume (`pgdata`) is moved by:

```bash
node scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs -- docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml
```

It dumps the old cluster with the old image in a throwaway container, starts the new server, restores the dump with every owner kept, and compares the row counts. The old volume stays until you remove it; the test database is created again by `node scripts/test-db.mjs`. Run `staff.js audit-verify` with every kept place before and after a major upgrade; Before going public says why.

## Upgrading

Authorities' orders and the alert channel (sub-project 3f) add a database role for the contact point's watcher, two services under a Compose profile, the hand-over's service under another, the report hold, and two arguments of the web build.

- On a database that exists, give the role its password and create it, with its USAGE on the schema `public`, once, as the superuser and against korbat's own database, before the first 3f migration: set `KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD` in `infra/.env` (`node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` does in development), run `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d postgres`, which passes it to the database's container, then the command below. Run twice, it changes nothing. The grant cannot be made by the migration: the migrator does not own the schema, and its grant would be a warning and nothing more. The migration checks both and stops with "create the role korbat_notify first" when either is missing, so a half-done upgrade stops there and not at a watcher that cannot read a row. A new data directory gets both from `infra/postgres/init/01-roles.sh`.

```bash
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml exec -T postgres sh -c 'psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -v pw="$KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD"' <<'SQL'
SET korbat.notify_pw = :'pw';
DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'korbat_notify') THEN
  IF current_setting('korbat.notify_pw') = '' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD is empty in the postgres container: set it in infra/.env, then up -d postgres'; END IF;
  EXECUTE format('CREATE ROLE korbat_notify LOGIN PASSWORD %L', current_setting('korbat.notify_pw'));
END IF; END $$;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO korbat_notify;
SQL
```

- `notify` and ntfy run under the Compose profile `notify`. Switch it on in one place, `COMPOSE_PROFILES=notify` in `infra/.env`, which Compose reads for every command: the README's commands stay as they are, and an upgrade then recreates the two services with the rest. Without that line they are never started, or keep running an old image against a migrated database.
- Until the contact-point mailbox exists, leave the profile off and set `API_NOTIFY=off`: korbat then says on the console's home screen that phone alerts are switched off on this server, and mails no "Phone alerts are down". No setting of `notify`, ntfy or the hand-over is needed for the stack to start.
- The quarantine's service (`quarantine`, sub-project 3d) runs under the Compose profile `quarantine`, which stays off: the operator starts it by hand with the steps under Quarantine. Its volume `media-quarantine` is created by its first run, owned by the API image's user; the hand-over's service now mounts it too, read-only. It needs no setting, and nothing of it is backed up.
- The hand-over's service (`handover`) runs under the Compose profile `handover`, which stays off: the operator starts it by hand for one hand-over, with the directory on its command line (Authorities' orders, Notifications and hand-overs). It needs no setting.
- The report hold is on from the upgrade: while a report of sealed images to the authorities is owed, the deletion of the account keeps its address, and nothing else, for at most 7 days. `API_REPORT_HOLD=off` in `infra/.env` ends the practice for everyone and deletes as before; set it only on counsel's advice.
- The web build takes `WEB_CONTACT_POINT` and `WEB_HOME_STATE` from `infra/.env` for the terms (the contact point for authorities and korbat's Member State). Neither is required, and both stay empty, or the state alone set, until the last step of Before going public; `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` adds the two lines to an existing file without changing a value. Rebuild the caddy image after a change of either.

## Backups

The backup of `media-store` is deleted 30 days after it was taken (`RETENTION.backupDays`, which the terms publish), without exception but an authority's written demand. `media-quarantine` is never backed up (Quarantine, step 4).

## Restoring

Restore the database and the `media-store` volume from the same moment. Keep the `media-store` volume as it was before the restore (copy it aside) until the Quarantine steps of Restoring the releases below have run: a file that a lifted seal returned from the quarantine after the backup is in that copy and in neither restored place. `counts` holds nothing to restore: its running month reads "not recorded". The API's sweeper deletes images that have no row: after a database restored from an older snapshot it would delete every image posted since. It refuses when there are many such images, but for a restore window set `MEDIA_RECONCILE=off` in `infra/.env` before starting the API, and put it back to `on` once the store matches the database. `force` makes one pass delete them anyway, for when they really are orphans.

Keep no backup of the database or of `media-store` more than 30 days after it was taken (`RETENTION.backupDays`, which the terms publish), and delete older ones, except a backup that korbat must keep for the authorities (step 5), which you keep until they have answered. A backup holds what korbat erased after it was taken, among it content erased under rule R4.

The staff steps run with the api service stopped (`docker compose -f infra/compose.yml stop api`), before it starts again, with the commands under Staff console and Moderation; step 5 says which of its parts wait until the API runs again:

1. Run `staff.js audit-head` on the restored database. Its place and hash go to the keeper with the restore's date: new rows will take the places lost with the backup's later rows, with other hashes, so every place kept after the backup would fail as a rewrite does. The keeper retires those places with that note, `audit-verify` runs from then on with the places at or before the restored one, and a failing place that no announced restore explains is a rewrite.
2. Run `staff.js revoke <email> all` for every account `staff.js keys` lists, since the restore brings back every staff key, staff session and enrolment link revoked or cancelled after the backup, and the auth events and audit rows that recorded those revocations are gone with it.
3. Run grant-role for every staff account with the role on your own list, and `user` for any other account `staff.js keys` lists, as after an API incident: it sets back any role changed after the backup and ends every session and staff session of the account, app sessions revoked after the backup included. Then compare the accounts `staff.js keys` lists with that list.
4. Each person enrols again, two keys each.
5. Moderation. Every decision, review and seal confirmed after the backup is gone with its audit rows, and what it restricted is back: sealed images are served again, and a removed post is public again. Reports, notices and re-examinations received after the backup are gone too, and so is everything `staff.js` wrote since: links and unlinks and limits. So are the stops that people pressed on a report's page after the backup, and the report mail that accounts resumed in Settings since; korbat may mail such an address about reports again, though its holder asked it to stop, until they press stop again, and an account that resumed its report mail gets none until it resumes again. Nothing on the server or in your records names them, so none can be applied again. Nothing on the restored server names the lost decisions either: the keeper's daily copy names them, and the orders and records to authorities, up to the keeper's last download, and Restoring with the keeper's copy below takes each lost measure again from it. So before the api service starts again after step 3, set `APP_SITE=closed` in `infra/.env` and recreate Caddy alone with `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d --no-deps caddy` (Caddy reads the setting only when it is created, and without `--no-deps` Compose would start the API with it), which closes the app's site and leaves the console's open, as that block's first step says; check from outside that the app's hostname answers 503. Before it starts, also delete the moderation dispatch's daily markers, which live in Valkey and are not restored with the database: `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml exec -T redis sh -c 'export VALKEYCLI_AUTH="$REDIS_PASSWORD"; valkey-cli --scan --pattern "*moderation-dispatched:*" | while read -r k; do valkey-cli del "$k"; done'`. The dispatch's first round then releases again every outcome and changed outcome that was answered before the day's dispatch hour and not yet released at the backup, so the status pages, the re-examination windows and the mails agree again; a person whose outcome mail or statement went out after the backup's time gets it a second time. Before it starts, also set `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=off` in `infra/.env`, which the API reads when `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api` starts it. The restored database no longer holds the cases, freezes and seals made after the backup. From its first round, 10 minutes after the start, the retention job would make R4 redactions final, erase case evidence and delete the images that these cases, freezes and seals no longer protect. That includes images sealed and reported to the police since the backup, long before an admin has enrolled and sealed them again. While the switch is off nothing is erased or deleted but the fingerprints and ratings of an automated tool that is off (Automated tools), and the console's count of late erasures rises. Before anyone decides anything, run `staff.js link` and `staff.js unlink` until the links match your records, and check that the count `staff.js keys` prints for each staff account equals your records'; then run `staff.js limits` with the numbers you last set. Once the staff have enrolled again, an admin first opens a finding citing R2 on every post or account that your R2 records show was sealed after the backup's time, unless its case is open in the restored database, and seals its images again. Only then, once every such seal has been applied again, set `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on` in `infra/.env` and run `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api`, which recreates the API with it, and open the app's site again when the console's After a restore screen says so (`APP_SITE=open`, then `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d --no-deps caddy api worker`: the API and the worker read the setting only when they start, and refuse a `test` adapter on an open site). Its next rounds make up the erasures that fell due meanwhile. Then tell the authority each of these was reported to what was lost and when it was sealed again, and keep the backup you restored from until that authority has answered, also past the 30 days. Sub-project 3d adds the release of sealed images and its replay after a restore. Then the cases that were open at the backup are open again in the queue: decide them again at once, lane 0 first. Each moderator also opens a finding on any other target they remember restricting since the backup's time.

**Restoring with the keeper's copy** (sub-project 3f). The keeper's daily copy of the audit log's tail (Staff console, the audit log's "Download since my last copy") names the orders, the records to authorities and the decisions the backup lacks, up to the keeper's last download. These steps come after the staff steps above; where they and step 5 differ, these hold.

1. Before the API starts: `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=off`, `MEDIA_RECONCILE=off` and `APP_SITE=closed` in `infra/.env`, which the API reads when `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api` starts it in step 5; then recreate Caddy alone with `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d --no-deps caddy`, since Caddy reads `APP_SITE` only when it is created, and check from outside that the app's hostname answers 503 to every path (`curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://<app hostname>/`); the console's site is unchanged.
2. Feed the import every keeper's file from the one that holds the restored head's place onward, oldest first, concatenated on standard input: `cat <files> | docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js restore-import <kept places>` (`-T`: without it Compose attaches a terminal and the redirect fails). The files need not start at the head: the import checks the earlier lines and skips them. A changed file is refused whole and nothing is written; a hole between two files is printed, and what lies behind it is not imported. Read what it prints, a hole among it.
3. Compare the contact-point mailbox since the keeper's last download with the orders it lists; open what is missing with `order-open --received`. An imported item whose link named no post shows `sha256:` and a digest in place of the link, since the copy holds no link's text: read the address from the order in the mailbox. Enter the records of class "record" again from the authority's letters, each with its command and `--gap <gap>`, which closes that gap. Until the last of them is entered, answer no data request: `access-request` cannot print an authority's "not to the person" mark for a record that is still lost.
4. Still before the API starts, record the restore of the audit log's daily value: `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js head-restore-mark <day>:<value> ...`, with the values of the keeper's mails for the days after the backup, each a day and its value as the mail gives them. Each is shown on `/transparency` as retired, every published value that the restored log no longer gives is retired too, none is deleted, and today's row says that korbat restored its database from a backup and which value is the last that still fits. Run it before the API starts: the API's first round after the dispatch hour would otherwise alert that the day before has no value and publish today's from the restored chain, which the keeper's mail of today no longer matches. Before any order's disabling is taken again: compare each held notice the import lists with the mailbox since the keeper's last download. An extension or a later time that was recorded after that download is lost with the restore; record it again first (`order-hold-extend`, `order-hold-until`), or the disabling taken again would tell the author at the old end.
5. Start the API with `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api`; everyone enrols new keys.
6. On the console's After a restore screen, take every measure again, from the top. An order's disabling first: its hour, its preservation and its hold are the old ones. A gap that needs nothing is closed by an admin as "Not needed", with the key.
7. When the screen says so, set `APP_SITE=open` and recreate Caddy, the API and the worker with `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d --no-deps caddy api worker` (the API and the worker read it only when they start, and refuse a `test` adapter on an open site), then check from outside that the app's hostname no longer answers 503; when it says so, switch retention and the sweep back on (`API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on`, `MEDIA_RECONCILE=on`) and run `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api`, since the API reads both only when it starts.

The keeper's file holds no post and no statement, but it names authorities and references, held orders' among them, and a reference may itself name a person: keep it like the head, not like a log.

**Restoring the releases** (sub-project 3d). While the app's site stays closed (step 1 above), after `restore-import` (step 2 above), which writes a gap of the class "Releases and held uploads to replay" for every release, every leave recorded and every leave withdrawn that the backup lacks:

1. `cat <the keeper's files> | docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js release-replay`. Every release recorded after the backup is marked again, for sealed posts and for held uploads: its posts are released and their image rows erased, a seal for good taken again afterwards freezes nothing, and a held upload whose refusal the backup does not hold is kept from every post. A replay whose author must not be told yet, or whose leave the restore lost, waits until it may be told. It passes over every line the restored database holds, takes the lines above it in their order, and prints a note and exits 1 only for what is still owed: a line no gap names, or a lost end of a hold whose refusal is there and whose gap is open, which an admin ends again (step 3). Each replay is a release of its own id: `release-show` takes the replay's own id, which `release-replay` prints, and answers no release for the original's.
2. Run the Quarantine steps 1 to 3 (list, move, record), then step 6 (the inventory), then steps 1 to 3 again. The first run moves into the quarantine what the restored store holds again of images sealed for good; the inventory gives a file the quarantine holds without a record its row, and its record reports each file recorded in the quarantine that it did not list: look for that file in the `media-store` kept from before the restore and put it back in the quarantine under its name before anything else, and record it lost (step 5) only when it is in neither. When the inventory's receipt is empty, skip its step 3: `quarantine-record` refuses an empty receipt. The second run's destroy lines name every released file that the restored store or the quarantine holds again. An `operator` line is a file the quarantine holds for an image the restored database does not know: never destroy it on that line alone; find the row of the keeper's files that names the image (`upload_hold_ended`, `upload_released`, `seal_released`). If it is held for a report, it stays where it is, and the operator's R2 records say so. If it was released, no list will ever print a `destroy` line for it, since the database cannot tie the file to its release: write that one line by hand (the `operator` line with `destroy` as its direction), run steps 2 and 3 with it, and note it.
3. On After a restore, a person closes what no command can: a lost end of a hold whose refusal is there is ended again by an admin, the same way (do not run `upload-report` a second time before the keeper's files have been checked for the record of the report); a measure a program had taken is taken again by a person, as 3f's classes say. A lost leave is recorded again from what korbat holds in writing, with `release-leave <seal> ... --gap <gap>`, which records it under the id the gap names and closes the gap. A lost withdrawal of a leave comes before anything else on its case: the restored database shows the mistaken leave as standing, so withdraw it again with `release-leave --withdraw <leave> --operator <name> --gap <gap>` before an admin reads the case.
The site opens only when After a restore shows no gap, the class "Releases and held uploads to replay" included, and `head-restore-mark` has run (step 4 of Restoring with the keeper's copy).

**The public figures after a restore** (sub-project 3d). A backup holds the yearly editions published and the months of the readers' count closed until it was taken, and nothing after. `restore-import` prints one line for each published version of an edition that the restored database lacks ("edition <year> version <n>, published <time>, is not in the restored database"), and writes nothing for it: `/transparency` no longer shows that version. The job publishes a year's first version again in its next daily round, computed from the restored database as of the same 1 March, which lacks what the backup lacked, and a version for an order whose hold ended again when it finds that order; a lost correction comes back only with `staff.js edition <year> --correct`. Note in the operator's notes each lost version, its day and, if you kept the page, how the new one differs, and say so to anyone who asks about it. A month closed after the backup is lost the same way, its two numbers with it (`recipient_months`), and no line or audit row records that it was: it reads "not recorded" in `staff.js recipients` and in the recipients' line of the next edition. Note the months between the backup and the restore.

A suspect or revoked staff key is never cleared or revived.

## Posting and feed
Text posts up to 1000 characters, replies, quotes, likes, reposts and bookmarks; follows, blocks and mutes; a chronological Following timeline and a public Latest timeline; threads and profile pages. The web app's home is the timeline; sign-in lives at `/signin`.

- **Reading signed out:** Latest, threads and profiles are public. Following, bookmarks, likes, follower lists and privacy settings need a session.
- **Blocks** are enforced in every query, not just the interface: neither account sees the other while signed in, follows are removed both ways, and the blocked side gets `not_found` so nothing is revealed. Posts are public, so a block does not hide them from someone who signs out; the interface says so.
- **Mutes** are one-way and silent, and hide an account from your timelines only.
- **Liker lists are never exposed.** Counts are public; likes and bookmarks are private to their owner.
- **Write limits** per account, tiered by account age: in the first 24 hours 5 posts and 20 replies an hour and no reposts or quotes for 48 hours; afterwards 30 posts and 60 replies an hour. Everyone: 100 likes an hour, 50 follows an hour and 400 a day, 30 blocks or mutes an hour. Undo actions are never limited.
- **Deleting** blanks the text in the database and leaves a tombstone only where a thread or a quote needs it. There is no editing. A post that a report or a moderator's finding named before it was deleted keeps a copy with its case, read by staff only, for as long as the case needs it (Moderation, Evidence and retention).
- **Moderation states.** A post is `visible`, `withheld` (while a case about it is being decided) or `removed`, as the database derives it from the measures that moderators' decisions recorded; nothing else writes the state, and the API's role cannot. A withheld or removed post is shown to its author alone, with a chip ("Under review" in amber, "Removed" in red) that names the rule or says "illegal content" and links to the decision's statement under Settings, Cases; everyone else finds it in no list and gets `not_found` for it.

## Images
Posts, replies and quotes can carry up to four images, and every image needs a description of up to 1000 characters. The web composer takes JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF and still GIF files up to 20 MB, and refuses HEIC with advice to export a JPEG.

- **Nothing of the original is kept**, but, while the known material check is switched on, three hashes of the file as received, deleted with the image or when the check is switched off; a match record keeps one of them for 180 days (Automated tools).
````
