import { createHmac, randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import type Redis from "ioredis";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import { RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES, RECIPIENT_RULES } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { clientNetwork } from "../auth";
import type { TransparencyRepo } from "./repo";

/**
 * The recipients' count (3d design, section 2 row 8 and section 7.5), method 1. It counts in sketches that hold no
 * member: a HyperLogLog in Valkey answers "about how many different values were added" and cannot give one back. 3d review
 * H3: the Valkey is the counts store of its own (COUNTS_URL), which writes nothing to disk, so the salt is written nowhere
 * else indeed, and no file keeps a value that was added to a sketch.
 *
 *   A, signed in: every request whose session resolved adds the account's id to `mau:in:<yyyy-mm>`, the UTC month's sketch.
 *   B, signed out (only while RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT is on): a GET of one of the seven public reads of the social module
 *      without a session adds HMAC-SHA-256(the day's salt, network LF user agent) to `mau:out:<yyyy-mm-dd>`, the network
 *      being clientNetwork(address) and the agent cut at 256 bytes. The salt, `mau:salt:<yyyy-mm-dd>`, is 32 random bytes
 *      set once with SET NX and 26 hours to live, kept in memory for its UTC day and written nowhere else, so after 26
 *      hours nobody, korbat included, can compute a digest again. An agent that names itself a crawler is left out; nothing
 *      else is guessed about a reader.
 *
 * Neither call is waited for, and every failure of Valkey is swallowed: counting never fails or slows a request. Every
 * sketch dies 70 days after its first write if the month's close never took it. The close, the transparency job's step on
 * its first round after a UTC month ended, stores two numbers in recipient_months and deletes the month's keys.
 */

/** The part of the Valkey client the sketches use. */
export type SketchStore = Pick<Redis, "pfadd" | "pfcount" | "expire" | "set" | "getBuffer" | "exists" | "del">;

/** What the auth module's resolveSession calls (section 5, `auth.onSeen`); both return at once and never throw. */
export interface RecipientCounter {
  /** A request whose session resolved. */
  seen(accountId: string): void;
  /** A request without a session: counted only for a GET of one of RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES, and only while the setting is on. */
  seenSignedOut(address: string, userAgent: string, path: string): void;
}

/** The UTC month of an instant, yyyy-mm. */
const monthOf = (at: Date) => at.toISOString().slice(0, 7);
/** The UTC day of an instant, yyyy-mm-dd. */
const dayOf = (at: Date) => at.toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/**
 * The three kinds of key the count writes, and no other (invariant 23); 3d review M10: and the job's mark of a month,
 * which holds the time the job first saw it and nothing of a person.
 */
export const sketchKeys = {
  month: (month: string) => `mau:in:${month}`,
  day: (day: string) => `mau:out:${day}`,
  salt: (day: string) => `mau:salt:${day}`,
  since: (month: string) => `mau:since:${month}`,
};

/**
 * The seven reads as patterns of a GET's path: a parameter matches one segment. Built once from the contracts' list,
 * which names the routes with their method.
 */
const READ_PATHS: readonly RegExp[] = RECIPIENT_READ_ROUTES.map((route) => {
  const path = route.slice(route.indexOf(" ") + 1);
  const pattern = path
    .split("/")
    .map((segment) => (segment.startsWith(":") ? "[^/]+" : segment))
    .join("/");
  return new RegExp(`^${pattern}$`);
});

/** Whether a GET of this path is one of the seven public reads. */
export const isReadRoute = (path: string) => READ_PATHS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(path));

const LF = Buffer.from([10]);
const SKETCH_SECONDS = RECIPIENT_RULES.sketchDays * 86_400;
const SALT_SECONDS = RECIPIENT_RULES.saltHours * 3_600;

export interface RecipientsDeps {
  store: SketchStore;
  /** RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT: whether signed-out readers are counted. */
  signedOut: boolean;
  log: Logger;
  now?: () => Date;
}

/** The two calls the auth module makes, over the store; each failure is logged at debug and dropped. */
export function createRecipientCounter(deps: RecipientsDeps): RecipientCounter {
  const now = deps.now ?? (() => new Date());
  // The day's salt, read or set once a UTC day and kept as a promise, so the requests of a new day's first moment share
  // one SET NX. A failure forgets it, and the next request asks again.
  let salt: { day: string; value: Promise<Buffer> } | null = null;
  const daySalt = (day: string): Promise<Buffer> => {
    if (salt?.day === day) return salt.value;
    const value = (async () => {
      const key = sketchKeys.salt(day);
      await deps.store.set(key, randomBytes(32), "EX", SALT_SECONDS, "NX");
      const stored = await deps.store.getBuffer(key);
      if (stored === null || stored.length !== 32) throw new Error("the day's salt could not be read back");
      return stored;
    })();
    salt = { day, value };
    value.catch(() => {
      if (salt?.value === value) salt = null;
    });
    return value;
  };
  /** Adds one value to a sketch and gives the sketch its days to live from its first write. */
  const add = async (key: string, value: string) => {
    await deps.store.pfadd(key, value);
    await deps.store.expire(key, SKETCH_SECONDS, "NX");
  };
  const swallow = (err: unknown) => deps.log.debug({ err }, "recipients: a count was not recorded");
  return {
    seen(accountId) {
      try {
        add(sketchKeys.month(monthOf(now())), accountId).catch(swallow);
      } catch (err) {
        swallow(err);
      }
    },
    seenSignedOut(address, userAgent, path) {
      if (!deps.signedOut || !isReadRoute(path) || RECIPIENT_RULES.crawler.test(userAgent)) return;
      try {
        const day = dayOf(now());
        const agent = Buffer.from(userAgent, "utf8").subarray(0, RECIPIENT_RULES.userAgentBytes);
        const network = Buffer.from(clientNetwork(address), "utf8");
        daySalt(day)
          .then((key) => add(sketchKeys.day(day), createHmac("sha256", key).update(Buffer.concat([network, LF, agent])).digest("hex")))
          .catch(swallow);
      } catch (err) {
        swallow(err);
      }
    },
  };
}

/** The months before the current one that a close looks at: two, since a sketch lives 70 days. */
const CLOSE_MONTHS = 2;

/**
 * 3d review M10: one round of the transparency job, the most a month's mark may lag its first instant: a round starts ten
 * minutes after the last one ended, and a round's lock lives twenty, which bounds when the month's first round must have
 * marked it. A mark later than this means the store lost the month's first part.
 */
export const MARK_WITHIN_MS = 20 * 60_000;

/**
 * 3d review M10: the job's mark of the running month, set once (SET NX) with a sketch's time to live: the instant the job
 * first saw the month. A store lost in the middle of the month loses the mark with the sketch, and the job's next round
 * marks the month again at a later instant, which tells the month's close that the sketch holds only the month's last part.
 */
export async function markMonth(store: SketchStore, at: Date): Promise<void> {
  await store.set(sketchKeys.since(monthOf(at)), at.toISOString(), "EX", SKETCH_SECONDS, "NX");
}

/** Whether the month's mark says the job saw the month from its start: set, and within one round of its first instant. */
async function wholeMonth(store: SketchStore, month: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const mark = await store.getBuffer(sketchKeys.since(month));
  if (mark === null) return false;
  const since = Date.parse(Buffer.isBuffer(mark) ? mark.toString("utf8") : String(mark));
  return Number.isFinite(since) && since <= Date.parse(`${month}-01T00:00:00.000Z`) + MARK_WITHIN_MS;
}

/** The first day of the month `back` months before the instant's own, as yyyy-mm. */
function monthBefore(at: Date, back: number): string {
  return monthOf(new Date(Date.UTC(at.getUTCFullYear(), at.getUTCMonth() - back, 1)));
}

/** Every day of a month (yyyy-mm), as yyyy-mm-dd. */
function daysOf(month: string): string[] {
  const [year, monthNumber] = month.split("-").map(Number) as [number, number];
  const last = new Date(Date.UTC(year, monthNumber, 0)).getUTCDate();
  return Array.from({ length: last }, (_, at) => `${month}-${String(at + 1).padStart(2, "0")}`);
}

/**
 * The month's close (7.5 step 3): for each of the two months before the current one whose signed-in sketch exists and
 * that recipient_months does not hold yet, the sketch's count and, while the setting is on, the sum of its days' counts
 * are stored, and then the month's keys are deleted. A month without a sketch gets no row: it reads as not recorded.
 * 3d review M10: so does a month whose mark is missing or later than one round after its first instant, since its
 * sketch then counts only what came after the store was lost; its keys go all the same. Answers the months it stored.
 */
export async function closeMonths(deps: { store: SketchStore; repo: Pick<TransparencyRepo, "monthStored" | "storeMonth">; signedOut: boolean }, at: Date): Promise<string[]> {
  const closed: string[] = [];
  for (let back = CLOSE_MONTHS; back >= 1; back--) {
    const month = monthBefore(at, back);
    const monthKey = sketchKeys.month(month);
    if ((await deps.store.exists(monthKey)) === 0) continue;
    const dayKeys = daysOf(month).map(sketchKeys.day);
    // A row stored by an earlier round that stopped before its delete: the keys go now, and the row stays as it was.
    if (!(await deps.repo.monthStored(month)) && (await wholeMonth(deps.store, month))) {
      const signedIn = await deps.store.pfcount(monthKey);
      let signedOutDays: number | null = null;
      if (deps.signedOut) {
        signedOutDays = 0;
        for (const key of dayKeys) signedOutDays += await deps.store.pfcount(key);
      }
      if (await deps.repo.storeMonth({ month, signedIn, signedOutDays, method: RECIPIENT_RULES.method })) closed.push(month);
    }
    // The row is stored: the sketches are no longer needed, and the days' salts died after their 26 hours.
    await deps.store.del(monthKey, ...dayKeys, sketchKeys.since(month));
  }
  return closed;
}

import { desc, eq, lt, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { ALERT_KINDS, HEAD_RULES, type EditionReason, type HeadKind, type HeadWitness, type TransparencyFigures } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { recipientMonths, transparencyEditions, type Db } from "@korbat/db";
import type { HeadDayRow, HeadToday } from "./head";

/**
 * The transparency module's statements (3d design, sections 6.4, 6.5, 7.5, 7.6 and 7.7). It names the three tables of
 * public record and nothing of a person (the architecture test holds every file of the module to the names of
 * schema/transparency.ts and the audit head): the editions it reads and has edition_publish() write, the months it reads
 * and inserts, and the head's daily rows, whose every forced column the database writes. Raw SQL reaches two tables of
 * other modules, as media/repo.ts reaches the outbox: alert_outbox, for the job's own two alerts, and audit_log's hash at
 * one place, for the keeper's mail when the head has moved on since the day's row was written.
 */

/** One stored version of a year's edition, as the public route reads it. */
export interface EditionRow {
  year: number;
  version: number;
  publishedAt: Date;
  method: number;
  reason: EditionReason;
  figures: TransparencyFigures;
}

/** One month of the recipients' count. */
export interface MonthRow {
  month: string;
  signedIn: number;
  signedOutDays: number | null;
  method: number;
}

/** How long a statement of the job waits for a lock: the job's other rounds are minutes away. */
const LOCK_TIMEOUT = sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`;

/** The database's UTC day, which the head's insert trigger stamps on the day's row. */
const TODAY = sql`(now() at time zone 'UTC')::date`;

export function createTransparencyRepo(apiDb: Db) {
  return {
    /** Every stored version of every year, newest year first and, inside a year, newest version first. */
    async editions(): Promise<EditionRow[]> {
      const rows = await apiDb
        .select({
          year: transparencyEditions.year,
          version: transparencyEditions.version,
          publishedAt: transparencyEditions.publishedAt,
          method: transparencyEditions.method,
          reason: transparencyEditions.reason,
          figures: transparencyEditions.figures,
        })
        .from(transparencyEditions)
        .orderBy(desc(transparencyEditions.year), desc(transparencyEditions.version));
      return rows.map((row) => ({ ...row, reason: row.reason as EditionReason, figures: row.figures as TransparencyFigures }));
    },

    /** The years before `before` that have an edition: a hold that ends after its year closed still gives it a version. */
    async yearsWithEdition(before: number): Promise<number[]> {
      const rows = await apiDb
        .selectDistinct({ year: transparencyEditions.year })
        .from(transparencyEditions)
        .where(lt(transparencyEditions.year, before))
        .orderBy(desc(transparencyEditions.year));
      return rows.map((row) => row.year);
    },

    /**
     * edition_publish(year, 'first') in a transaction of its own, since its audit row holds the chain's head until the
     * commit: the version it wrote, or null when nothing was due or new. The function decides; the job only asks.
     */
    publish(year: number): Promise<number | null> {
      return apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(LOCK_TIMEOUT);
        const [row] = await tx.execute<{ version: number | null }>(sql`select public.edition_publish(${year}::int, 'first') as version`);
        return row?.version ?? null;
      });
    },

    /** Whether a month (yyyy-mm) is stored already. */
    async monthStored(month: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const [row] = await apiDb.select({ month: recipientMonths.month }).from(recipientMonths).where(eq(recipientMonths.month, `${month}-01`)).limit(1);
      return row !== undefined;
    },

    /**
     * 7.7 step 2: the day's head row, inserted once (on conflict, nothing) with the witness's name and nothing else, since
     * the trigger forces the rest from audit_head; then the day's row as it stands, in the same transaction, so both read
     * the database's today at one instant.
     */
    headInsert(witness: HeadWitness): Promise<HeadToday> {
      return apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(LOCK_TIMEOUT);
        const inserted = await tx.execute(sql`insert into public.head_publications (witness) values (${witness}) on conflict (day, kind) do nothing returning 1`);
        const [row] = await tx.execute<{ day: string; value: string; witness: HeadWitness; witnessed: boolean; published: boolean; mailed: boolean }>(sql`
          select to_char(h.day, 'YYYY-MM-DD') as day, h.value, h.witness, h.token is not null as witnessed, h.published_at is not null as published,
                 h.keeper_mailed_at is not null as mailed
            from public.head_publications h where h.day = ${TODAY} and h.kind = 'head'`);
        return { inserted: inserted.length > 0, ...row! };
      });
    },

    /** 7.7 step 3: the witness's token, set from null alone (the guard refuses a second); false when the row had one. */
    async headWitnessed(day: string, token: Uint8Array): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await apiDb.execute(sql`
        update public.head_publications set token = ${Buffer.from(token)}, witnessed_at = now()
         where day = ${day}::date and kind = 'head' and token is null returning 1`);
      return rows.length > 0;
    },

    /** 7.7 step 4: published, from null, once: whether a token is stored, or null when an earlier round published it. */
    async headPublish(day: string): Promise<{ witnessed: boolean } | null> {
      const [row] = await apiDb.execute<{ witnessed: boolean }>(sql`
        update public.head_publications set published_at = now()
         where day = ${day}::date and kind = 'head' and published_at is null returning token is not null as witnessed`);
      return row ?? null;
    },

    /**
     * 7.7 step 5: the place the day's value was computed from and that place's hash, read from the head while it still
     * stands there or from the audit log's row of that place, and only when head_value() of the day, the place and the
     * hash gives the stored value; null otherwise, and then the keeper is not mailed.
     */
    async headPlace(day: string): Promise<{ seq: number; hash: string } | null> {
      const [row] = await apiDb.execute<{ seq: number; hash: string; fits: boolean }>(sql`
        select h.chain_seq::int as seq, x.hash, public.head_value(h.day, h.chain_seq, x.hash) = h.value as fits
          from public.head_publications h
          cross join lateral (
            select a.hash from public.audit_head a where a.id = 1 and a.seq = h.chain_seq
            union all
            select l.hash from public.audit_log l where l.chain_seq = h.chain_seq
            limit 1) x
         where h.day = ${day}::date and h.kind = 'head'`);
      return row?.fits ? { seq: row.seq, hash: row.hash } : null;
    },

    /** 3d review M13: the relay accepted the keeper's mail of the day's value: keeper_mailed_at, from null alone (the guard forces the time). */
    async headMailed(day: string): Promise<void> {
      await apiDb.execute(sql`update public.head_publications set keeper_mailed_at = now() where day = ${day}::date and kind = 'head' and keeper_mailed_at is null`);
    },

    /** 3d review M13: the day before the database's today, when its value was published and its keeper's mail never accepted; null otherwise. */
    async headUnmailed(): Promise<string | null> {
      const [row] = await apiDb.execute<{ day: string }>(sql`
        select to_char(h.day, 'YYYY-MM-DD') as day from public.head_publications h
         where h.kind = 'head' and h.day = ${TODAY} - 1 and h.published_at is not null and h.keeper_mailed_at is null`);
      return row?.day ?? null;
    },

    /**
     * 7.7 step 6: the day before the database's today, when it has no published head value while an earlier day has a
     * row; null otherwise. On the head's first day nothing is missed: no earlier day ever had a value.
     */
    async headMissed(): Promise<string | null> {
      const [row] = await apiDb.execute<{ day: string }>(sql`
        select to_char(${TODAY} - 1, 'YYYY-MM-DD') as day
         where not exists (select 1 from public.head_publications h where h.kind = 'head' and h.day = ${TODAY} - 1 and h.published_at is not null)
           and exists (select 1 from public.head_publications h where h.kind = 'head' and h.day < ${TODAY} - 1)`);
      return row?.day ?? null;
    },

    /**
     * The job's own alert head_unwitnessed or head_missed (7.14, "Alerts a job writes"): one row of the outbox with its
     * kind's priority and scope and its one fact, the day's first instant, under F's daily rule: none while a row of the
     * kind was written in the last 24 hours. F's two legs push and mail it. Answers whether it wrote one.
     */
    async headAlert(kind: "head_unwitnessed" | "head_missed" | "head_unmailed", day: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const entry = ALERT_KINDS[kind];
      const written = await apiDb.execute(sql`
        insert into public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, facts)
        select ${kind}, ${entry.priority}, ${entry.scope}, ${JSON.stringify({ day: `${day}T00:00:00.000Z` })}::jsonb
         where not exists (select 1 from public.alert_outbox o where o.kind = ${kind} and o.created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => 24))
        returning id`);
      return written.length > 0;
    },

    /**
     * GET /api/public/head's rows (10.6): the published rows of the last HEAD_RULES.shownDays days, today's included, newest
     * day first and, within a day, the latest published first. The place is not read.
     */
    async headDays(): Promise<HeadDayRow[]> {
      const rows = await apiDb.execute<{ day: string; kind: HeadKind; value: string; witness: HeadWitness; token: Buffer | null; retired_on: string | null; last_day: string | null }>(sql`
        select to_char(h.day, 'YYYY-MM-DD') as day, h.kind, h.value, h.witness, h.token,
               to_char(h.retired_at at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD') as retired_on, to_char(h.last_day, 'YYYY-MM-DD') as last_day
          from public.head_publications h
         where h.published_at is not null and h.day > ${TODAY} - ${HEAD_RULES.shownDays}::int
         order by h.day desc, h.published_at desc`);
      return rows.map((row) => ({ day: row.day, kind: row.kind, value: row.value, witness: row.witness, token: row.token, retiredOn: row.retired_on, lastDay: row.last_day }));
    },

    /** Stores a month's two numbers once; false when another round stored it first. computed_at is the database's. */
    async storeMonth(month: MonthRow): Promise<boolean> {
      // The API's role may insert these four columns and no other: the insert trigger forces computed_at.
      const rows = await apiDb.execute<{ month: string }>(sql`
        insert into public.recipient_months (month, signed_in, signed_out_days, method)
        values (${`${month.month}-01`}::date, ${month.signedIn}::int, ${month.signedOutDays}::int, ${month.method}::smallint)
        on conflict (month) do nothing returning month::text`);
      return rows.length > 0;
    },
  };
}

export type TransparencyRepo = ReturnType<typeof createTransparencyRepo>;

import { Hono } from "hono";
import type { PublicFacts } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { Config } from "../config";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import { publicTransparency } from "./editions";
import { publicHead } from "./head";
import type { TransparencyRepo } from "./repo";

/**
 * The public answers (3d design, sections 9.1 and 10.6), mounted at /api after the global rate limit and before the
 * session's resolution (app.ts), as the page status is: neither reads a session, a cookie or a table of a person.
 *
 *   GET /api/public/facts         what is switched on now, read from memory, Cache-Control: no-cache, so /rules prints
 *                                 what runs now, also in the minute after a restart;
 *   GET /api/public/transparency  every year's editions from transparency_editions, Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600:
 *                                 nothing in it changes within a day;
 *   GET /api/public/head          the audit head's published values of the last HEAD_RULES.shownDays days (Task 5), public
 *                                 for an hour too: a day gains its value once, after the dispatch hour, and never the place.
 */

/**
 * The facts of the running server (10.6): booleans, names, days and numbers, never a token, a zone, a host or an address.
 * The comparison with known material prints its state (3d Task 7); the edge prints its adapter
 * (Task 3), and the head's witness its own (Task 5), never its authority's address. A test adapter prints "on" and says it
 * is one. 3d Task 6: the R1 check prints its state (off; on and flagging; on and withholding, AUTOMATION_R1_ACTS), whether
 * it is the test scorer, and its two impact assessments' days, each in its own block; the model, its digest, its
 * threshold, its version and the publisher's claim stay null while no classifier is built in, which no build of 3d does.
 */
export function publicFacts(
  config: Pick<Config, "EDGE_PURGE" | "RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT" | "HEAD_WITNESS" | "R1_CLASSIFIER" | "AUTOMATION_R1_ACTS" | "AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1" | "AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1_ACTS"> &
    Partial<Pick<Config, "MEDIA_MATCH" | "AUTOMATION_R2_ACTS" | "AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH" | "AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH_ACTS" | "HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL">>,
): PublicFacts {
  // 3d Task 7 (sections 2 rows 27 and 49, 10.6): the comparison prints its state (off; on and only alerting, the finding
  // and the urgent alert; on and sealing, AUTOMATION_R2_ACTS), whether it is the test matcher, the source's name and its
  // two impact assessments' days, each in its own block. A source is named here only once it has allowed that; the test
  // matcher's name is "test".
  const match = config.MEDIA_MATCH ?? "off";
  const matchOn = match !== "off";
  const r1On = config.R1_CLASSIFIER !== "off";
  return {
    r1: {
      state: !r1On ? "off" : config.AUTOMATION_R1_ACTS === "on" ? "withholds" : "flags",
      test: config.R1_CLASSIFIER === "test",
      model: null,
      digest: null,
      threshold: null,
      thresholdVersion: null,
      publisherClaim: null,
      dpia: config.AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1 ?? null,
      dpiaActs: config.AUTOMATION_DPIA_R1_ACTS ?? null,
    },
    match: {
      state: !matchOn ? "off" : (config.AUTOMATION_R2_ACTS ?? "on") === "on" ? "seals" : "alerts",
      test: match === "test",
      source: matchOn ? match : null,
      dpia: config.AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH ?? null,
      dpiaActs: config.AUTOMATION_DPIA_MATCH_ACTS ?? null,
    },
    edge: { on: config.EDGE_PURGE !== "off", test: config.EDGE_PURGE === "test" },
    witness: { on: config.HEAD_WITNESS !== "off", test: config.HEAD_WITNESS === "test" },
    recipientsSignedOut: config.RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT === "on",
    // 3d review M13: whether the daily value goes to a keeper at all; never the address.
    keeper: config.HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL !== undefined && config.HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL !== "",
  };
}

export function transparencyRoutes(deps: { repo: Pick<TransparencyRepo, "editions" | "headDays">; facts: PublicFacts }) {
  const r = new Hono<AppEnv>();
  r.get("/public/facts", (c) => {
    c.header("Cache-Control", "no-cache");
    return c.json(deps.facts);
  });
  r.get("/public/transparency", async (c) => {
    const answer = publicTransparency(await deps.repo.editions());
    c.header("Cache-Control", "public, max-age=3600");
    return c.json(answer);
  });
  r.get("/public/head", async (c) => {
    const answer = publicHead(await deps.repo.headDays());
    c.header("Cache-Control", "public, max-age=3600");
    return c.json(answer);
  });
  return r;
}

import { useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { Platform, Pressable, ScrollView, Text, View } from "react-native";
import { ANNEX3_GROUNDS, ORDER_GROUNDS, PublicFacts, PublicHead, PublicTransparency, type OrderFigures, type TransparencyFigures } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AppShell } from "@/components/AppShell";
import { TextLink } from "@/components/ui";
import { api } from "@/lib/api";
import { saveBlob } from "@/lib/download";
import { PAGE_DOWN, TRANSPARENCY_PAGE, recipientsMonth } from "@/lib/public-pages";

const T = TRANSPARENCY_PAGE;
type Edition = PublicTransparency["editions"][number];
type Row = { label: string; count: string };

/** A heading of the page: level 2 a year or a fixed section, level 3 a table inside a year. */
function Heading({ level, children }: { level: 2 | 3; children: string }) {
  return (
    <Text accessibilityRole="header" aria-level={level} className={level === 2 ? "mt-8 text-lg font-semibold text-zinc-100" : "mt-5 text-base font-semibold text-zinc-100"}>
      {children}
    </Text>
  );
}
const Paragraph = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => <Text className="mt-2 text-base leading-7 text-zinc-300">{children}</Text>;

/**
 * One table: its heading and its rows, each read as "label: value" and laid out as a block, never a chart (9.1); a table
 * with no row is its "none" sentence.
 */
function Table({ title, rows }: { title: string; rows: Row[] }) {
  return (
    <View>
      <Heading level={3}>{title}</Heading>
      {rows.length === 0 ? (
        <Paragraph>{T.tableNone}</Paragraph>
      ) : (
        <View role="list" aria-label={title}>
          {rows.map((row) => (
            <Text key={row.label} role="listitem" className="mt-1 text-base leading-6 text-zinc-300">
              {`${row.label}: ${row.count}`}
            </Text>
          ))}
        </View>
      )}
    </View>
  );
}

/** A table's stored rows with the page's labels: `other` by the table's own word. */
const labelled = (rows: readonly { label: string; count: string }[], label: (key: string) => string, other: string): Row[] =>
  rows.map((row) => ({ label: row.label === "other" ? other : label(row.label), count: row.count }));

/** An order figure as the page prints it: a number, or "not recorded", never 0, for a figure the rows can no longer give. */
const figure = (n: number | null) => (n === null ? T.notRecorded : String(n));
const byGround = (grounds: readonly string[], counts: Record<string, number> | null) =>
  counts === null ? T.notRecorded : grounds.map((ground) => `${T.grounds[ground] ?? ground} ${counts[ground]}`).join(", ");

/**
 * The section on authorities' orders (9.3 item 4): [tr.orders], then the yearly report's headings with tco-counts'
 * figures as numbers, without the issuing state. It stands only in a year that has the section.
 */
function OrdersSection({ orders }: { orders: OrderFigures }) {
  const L = T.orderLines;
  const minutes = orders.minutes;
  const minutesList = minutes === null ? T.notRecorded : minutes.list.length === 0 ? "none" : minutes.list.map((n) => figure(n)).join(", ");
  return (
    <View>
      <Heading level={3}>{T.ordersHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{T.orders}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.received}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{orders.received === null ? L.received(T.notRecorded, T.notRecorded) : L.received(String(orders.received.total), String(orders.received.crossBorder))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.disabled}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.itemsDisabled(figure(orders.itemsDisabled))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.minutes(minutesList)}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.late}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.outside(minutes === null || minutes.withoutReceipt > 0 ? T.notRecorded : String(minutes.outside))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.open(minutes === null ? T.notRecorded : String(minutes.open))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.annex3(byGround(ANNEX3_GROUNDS, orders.annex3))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.scrutiny}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{orders.scrutiny === null ? L.scrutiny(T.notRecorded, T.notRecorded, T.notRecorded) : L.scrutiny(String(orders.scrutiny.requested), String(orders.scrutiny.annulled), String(orders.scrutiny.upheld))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.reinstated(byGround(ORDER_GROUNDS, orders.reinstated))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.orderHeadings.own}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.terrorist(String(orders.terroristWithoutOrder))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.access(figure(orders.authorityAccess))}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{L.referrals(String(orders.referralsClosed))}</Paragraph>
    </View>
  );
}

/** The tables of one version's figures, in W.2's order, then the order section, the standing sentence and the recipients. */
export function FiguresView({ year, figures }: { year: number; figures: TransparencyFigures }) {
  const r = figures.restrictions;
  const findings = labelled(figures.automated.findings, T.labels.findings, T.labels.other);
  const programs = [...findings, ...labelled(figures.automated.measures, T.labels.measures, T.labels.other)];
  const month = recipientsMonth(year);
  const recipients = figures.recipients;
  return (
    <View>
      <Table
        title={T.tables.byGround}
        rows={r.byGround.length === 0 ? [] : [...labelled(r.byGround, (key) => (key === "law" ? T.labels.law : T.labels.ground(key)), T.labels.otherGrounds), { label: T.labels.allRestrictions, count: r.total }]}
      />
      <Table title={T.tables.byMeasure} rows={labelled(r.byMeasure, T.labels.measure, T.labels.otherMeasures)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.noBreach} rows={[{ label: T.labels.noBreach, count: figures.noBreach }]} />
      <Table title={T.tables.intakes} rows={labelled(figures.intakes, (key) => T.labels.intakes[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.appeals} rows={labelled(figures.appeals, (key) => T.labels.appeals[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.reexaminations} rows={labelled(figures.reexaminations, (key) => T.labels.reexaminations[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.accountMeasures} rows={labelled(figures.accountMeasures, T.labels.measure, T.labels.otherMeasures)} />
      <Table title={T.tables.automated} rows={programs} />
      {figures.automated.r1 ? <Paragraph>{T.autoRate(figures.automated.r1.base, figures.automated.r1.restricted)}</Paragraph> : findings.length > 0 ? <Paragraph>{T.autoFew}</Paragraph> : null}
      {figures.uploads ? <Table title={T.tables.uploads} rows={labelled(figures.uploads, (key) => T.labels.uploads[key] ?? key, T.labels.other)} /> : null}
      {figures.orders ? <OrdersSection orders={figures.orders} /> : null}
      <Paragraph>{T.ordersHeld}</Paragraph>
      <Heading level={3}>{T.recipientsHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>
        {recipients === "not recorded" ? T.recipientsNotYet : recipients.high === undefined ? T.recipientsOff(month, recipients.low) : T.recipients(month, recipients.low, recipients.high)}
      </Paragraph>
    </View>
  );
}

/** An older version of a year: its line, and its figures opened in place. */
function OlderVersion({ year, older }: { year: number; older: Edition["older"][number] }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <View>
      <Paragraph>{T.versionLine(older.version, older.publishedOn, older.replacedOn)}</Paragraph>
      <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" onPress={() => setOpen(!open)} className="mt-1 self-start">
        <Text className="text-sm text-sky-400 underline">{open ? T.hideVersion : T.showVersion}</Text>
      </Pressable>
      {open ? <FiguresView year={year} figures={older.figures} /> : null}
    </View>
  );
}

/** One year's section (9.3 item 2): its newest version, why that version was made, and its older versions. */
function EditionView({ edition, newest }: { edition: Edition; newest: boolean }) {
  return (
    <View>
      <Heading level={2}>{String(edition.year)}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{T.edition(edition.year, edition.version, edition.publishedOn, edition.method)}</Paragraph>
      {edition.reason === "hold_ended" ? <Paragraph>{T.reason.hold_ended}</Paragraph> : null}
      {edition.reason === "correction" ? <Paragraph>{T.reason.correction(edition.publishedOn)}</Paragraph> : null}
      <FiguresView year={edition.year} figures={edition.figures} />
      {edition.older.length > 0 ? (
        <View>
          <Paragraph>{T.versions}</Paragraph>
          {edition.older.map((older) => (
            <OlderVersion key={older.version} year={edition.year} older={older} />
          ))}
        </View>
      ) : null}
      {newest ? <Paragraph>{T.method(edition.method)}</Paragraph> : null}
    </View>
  );
}

type HeadDay = PublicHead["days"][number];

/** A day before another, as the page prints a day. */
const dayBefore = (day: string) => new Date(Date.parse(`${day}T00:00:00.000Z`) - 86_400_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10);

/** One line of the head's section: a published row, or a day between two shown days that has no head value. */
type HeadLine = { kind: "row"; row: HeadDay } | { kind: "missing"; day: string };

/**
 * The section's lines (9.3 item 6): the rows newest first as the route gives them, and [tr.headMissing] for each day
 * between the newest and the oldest shown day that has no head value, after that day's restore row when it has one. A
 * day after the newest row is not shown as missing: its value may not be published yet.
 */
export function headLines(days: readonly HeadDay[]): HeadLine[] {
  const lines: HeadLine[] = [];
  const valued = new Set(days.filter((row) => row.kind === "head").map((row) => row.day));
  const newest = days[0]?.day;
  const oldest = days.at(-1)?.day;
  if (newest === undefined || oldest === undefined) return lines;
  for (let day = newest; day >= oldest; day = dayBefore(day)) {
    for (const row of days) if (row.day === day) lines.push({ kind: "row", row });
    if (!valued.has(day)) lines.push({ kind: "missing", day });
  }
  return lines;
}

/** A day's proof saved as <day>.tsr: the token as the authority sent it, the TimeStampResp that openssl reads. */
function saveProof(day: string, token: string) {
  const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(token), (char) => char.charCodeAt(0));
  saveBlob(new Blob([bytes], { type: "application/timestamp-reply" }), `${day}.tsr`);
}

/**
 * Section 6, the audit log's daily value (3d design, section 9.3 item 6; W.2; Task 5): [tr.head], then a row a day,
 * newest first, with its value and who witnessed it, a restore's row with [tr.restore], a retired value with
 * [tr.retired] and a day without a value with [tr.headMissing]; while a shown row has a proof, [tr.verify] with the newest
 * such day's value and file, and each day's proof to download on the web. When the route did not answer, this part alone
 * reads [page.down]. The place is in no answer and on no row.
 */
function HeadSection({ head, keeper }: { head: PublicHead | "loading" | "down"; keeper: boolean | null }) {
  const T = TRANSPARENCY_PAGE;
  const witnessed = head === "loading" || head === "down" ? undefined : head.days.find((row) => row.token !== null);
  // 3d review M13: the keeper's sentence only while the facts say a keeper's address is set; neither until they answer.
  const keeperSentence = keeper === null ? "" : ` ${keeper ? T.headKeeper : T.headNoKeeper}`;
  return (
    <View>
      <Heading level={2}>{T.headHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{`${T.head}${keeperSentence}`}</Paragraph>
      {head === "loading" ? null : head === "down" ? (
        <Paragraph>{PAGE_DOWN}</Paragraph>
      ) : head.days.length === 0 ? (
        <Paragraph>{T.headNone}</Paragraph>
      ) : (
        <View role="list" aria-label={T.headHeading}>
          {headLines(head.days).map((line) =>
            line.kind === "missing" ? (
              <Text key={`${line.day}-missing`} role="listitem" className="mt-1 text-base leading-6 text-zinc-300">
                {T.headMissingRow(line.day)}
              </Text>
            ) : (
              <View key={`${line.row.day}-${line.row.kind}`} role="listitem" className="mt-1">
                <Text className="break-all text-base leading-6 text-zinc-300">
                  {line.row.kind === "restore"
                    ? T.restore(line.row.day, line.row.lastDay)
                    : line.row.retiredOn === null
                      ? T.headRow(line.row.day, line.row.value, line.row.witness)
                      : `${T.headRow(line.row.day, line.row.value, line.row.witness)} ${T.retired(line.row.retiredOn)}`}
                </Text>
                {line.row.token !== null && Platform.OS === "web" ? (
                  <Pressable accessibilityRole="button" onPress={() => saveProof(line.row.day, line.row.token!)} className="mt-1 self-start">
                    <Text className="text-sm text-sky-400 underline">{T.download(line.row.day)}</Text>
                  </Pressable>
                ) : null}
              </View>
            ),
          )}
        </View>
      )}
      {witnessed ? <Paragraph>{T.verify(witnessed.value, witnessed.day)}</Paragraph> : null}
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * The transparency page as it reads with the editions and the head's values it was given (3d design, section 9.3; W.2).
 * It shows what the stored editions hold and never a live count: no year section for the running year, and [tr.none]
 * while no edition exists. When a route did not answer, the fixed texts stand and that route's part alone reads
 * [page.down].
 */
export function TransparencyView({ answer, head = "loading", keeper = null }: { answer: PublicTransparency | "loading" | "down"; head?: PublicHead | "loading" | "down"; keeper?: boolean | null }) {
  return (
    <View>
      <Text accessibilityRole="header" className="text-3xl font-bold tracking-tight text-zinc-50">
        {T.title}
      </Text>
      <Paragraph>{T.lead}</Paragraph>
      <Paragraph>{T.read}</Paragraph>
      {answer === "loading" ? null : answer === "down" ? (
        <Paragraph>{PAGE_DOWN}</Paragraph>
      ) : answer.editions.length === 0 ? (
        <Paragraph>{T.none}</Paragraph>
      ) : (
        answer.editions.map((edition, index) => <EditionView key={edition.year} edition={edition} newest={index === 0} />)
      )}
      <HeadSection head={head} keeper={keeper} />
      <Heading level={2}>{T.tdbHeading}</Heading>
      <Paragraph>{T.tdb}</Paragraph>
      <TextLink label={T.rulesLink} href="/rules" />
      <TextLink label={T.exploreLink} href="/explore/about" />
    </View>
  );
}

/**
 * /transparency (3d design, sections 9.1 and 9.3), public, signed in or out: it reads no session for its content and
 * sends two GETs, /api/public/transparency and (Task 5) /api/public/head, each of which may be an hour old: nothing in
 * them changes within a day. Each fails alone: the other part still shows. 3d review M13: and a third, /api/public/facts,
 * for whether a keeper's address is set, which alone lets [tr.head] say the value goes to a keeper.
 */
export default function TransparencyPage() {
  const [answer, setAnswer] = useState<PublicTransparency | "loading" | "down">("loading");
  const [head, setHead] = useState<PublicHead | "loading" | "down">("loading");
  const [keeper, setKeeper] = useState<boolean | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true;
    api("/api/public/facts", { schema: PublicFacts })
      .then((read) => {
        if (live) setKeeper(read.keeper);
      })
      .catch(() => {
        // Without the facts the page says neither sentence about the keeper.
        if (live) setKeeper(null);
      });
    api("/api/public/transparency", { schema: PublicTransparency })
      .then((read) => {
        if (live) setAnswer(read);
      })
      .catch(() => {
        if (live) setAnswer("down");
      });
    api("/api/public/head", { schema: PublicHead })
      .then((read) => {
        if (live) setHead(read);
      })
      .catch(() => {
        if (live) setHead("down");
      });
    return () => {
      live = false;
    };
  }, []);
  return (
    <AppShell>
      <ScrollView className="flex-1 bg-zinc-950" contentContainerClassName="px-4 pb-16 pt-6">
        <View className="w-full max-w-xl">
          <TransparencyView answer={answer} head={head} keeper={keeper} />
        </View>
      </ScrollView>
    </AppShell>
  );
}

    },
    { tool: "edge", on: edge.on, paragraphs: [edge.on ? marked(TOOL_TEXTS.edge.on, edge.test) : TOOL_TEXTS.edge.off] },
    // 3d review M13: the off text names the keeper's mail only while a keeper's address is set.
    { tool: "witness", on: witness.on, paragraphs: [witness.on ? marked(TOOL_TEXTS.witness.on, witness.test) : facts.keeper ? TOOL_TEXTS.witness.off : TOOL_TEXTS.witness.offAlone] },
  ];
}

/** The six full months before an edition's due day end with this month (yyyy-mm), the same in every version of the year. */
export function recipientsMonth(year: number): string {
  return new Date(Date.UTC(year + 1, TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueMonth - 1, 0)).toISOString().slice(0, 7);
}

const MONTHS = ["January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October", "November", "December"];
/** The day a year's edition is due, as a sentence names it: 1 March, from TRANSPARENCY_RULES. */
const DUE = `${TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueDay} ${MONTHS[TRANSPARENCY_RULES.dueMonth - 1]}`;
/** The floor and the rounding of a banded count, as a sentence names them. */
const FLOOR = numberWord(TRANSPARENCY_RULES.floor);
const UNDER_FLOOR = `1 to ${TRANSPARENCY_RULES.floor - 1}`;
const ROUND_TO = numberWord(TRANSPARENCY_RULES.roundTo);

/** Who witnessed a day's value, as its row says it. */
const HEAD_WITNESS_WORDS: Record<HeadWitness, string> = {
  rfc3161: "with an outside timestamp",
  test: "with a test adapter's timestamp, which proves nothing",
  none: "without an outside timestamp",
};

/** The labels of a measure in the tables: the ledger's own. */
const measureLabel = (kind: string) => (kind in MEASURES ? MEASURES[kind as MeasureKind].label : kind);
/** A rule's title in force, for the table by ground. */
const ruleTitle = (id: string) => RULES.find((rule) => rule.id === id)?.title ?? id;

The one exception is the section on authorities' orders: the law asks for those figures as numbers, so they are printed as numbers, small ones too. korbat publishes one edition for each calendar year, on or after ${DUE} of the next year, and never changes it: a correction is a new version beside it, marked and dated. The running year shows no figure, so nothing on this page moves when korbat takes one decision.`,

# korbat sub-project 3d: transparency and automation

Date: 2026-10-09. Status: design, written without the user with the lighter process of the 3e and 3f designs: an index of the scope and the gaps, three research files, one architect's model with its labs, three drafters, one review round by three reviewers (the ledger, SQL and files; the people, the law and the words; fit to the code, the adapters and the tasks: 62 findings, all applied, five of them in the form a ruling gave), a consistency pass and a last settling of four points. It expands the model `korbat-scratch/research-3d/model-3d.md`, which is decided; what the owner or counsel may overturn is flagged in section 2 and gathered in section 17. What the review round did not find is found when the code is built; the dry run's amendments will be added at the end as 3c's were.

It is the last design of sub-project 3 and builds on the three before it: the 3c design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-moderation-cases-3c-design.md`, cited as "3c" or "C" with its section), the 3e design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-account-sanctions-3e-design.md`, "3e" or "E") and the 3f design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-authorities-orders-3f-design.md`, "3f" or "F"); "M" with a line number is the main design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-korbat-design.md`). It changes none of their migrations. **Every part that needs a third party or a fetched artefact is behind an adapter that is off by default** (the edge cache's purge, the matching of uploads against a list of known material, the classifier for rule R1, an outside witness for the audit log's head): with all of them off, 3d still builds the public pages and counts, the quarantine of sealed image files, their release with its replay, the automated decision as a kind of its own, and the signals; what the owner must obtain, decide and sign before any adapter is switched on is section 17.

Research, in `korbat-scratch/research-3d/`: `inputs.md` (scope items D1 to D28, where the designs overtook the earlier research P3-1 to P3-24, gaps X1 to X18); `gap-X-transparency.md`, `gap-X-automation.md`, `gap-X-known-material.md`; the lab `lab-3d/` on PostgreSQL 18.6. The reviews, the rulings and the editors' logs are beside them.

## 1. Context

3c gave korbat cases, decisions that are the statement of reasons, a ledger from which every restriction is derived, and a freeze and a seal for suspected child sexual abuse material that nobody at korbat opens. 3e added the measures on an account. 3f added authorities' orders, the alert channel, the records of what korbat tells an authority, and the daily copy with its restore. Each of the three left the same things to 3d, and this design builds them.

**What is missing today**, in the scratch clone at `aab8345` and in the three designs:

- **Nothing is public.** The app has no `/rules` and no `/transparency` (`apps/app/src/app/` holds `explore/about.tsx`, `terms.tsx`, `report.tsx` and `notice/`). The rules are read only inside the report form and the terms. Migration 0014 dropped the old `transparency_log`, and no count of anything leaves the database. The audit log's head leaves the server only in the keeper's hands (3f).
- **A sealed image has no end and no safe place.** A seal for good ends only by a reversal (`measures_in_force`, `0015_greedy_zuras.sql:679`), so the files stay in `media-store`, which the API mounts and the worker writes. An API under an attacker's control can read any stored file and ask for any file's deletion (`apps/api/src/media/files.ts:178`, `:181`; C 11). After a restore nothing says which sealed images had been released, because nothing can release one.
- **A hidden image stays at the edge.** A public image is served with `public, max-age=300` (`apps/api/src/media/flows/serve.ts:6`), and no code tells a cache when a measure, an order or a deletion ends that.
- **No program can act, and none may.** `decisions.decided_by` is NOT NULL (`0015:136`), `decisions_record` forces `automated_decision` to `not_automated` (`0017_appeals.sql:169`), a finding needs a staff account, and `post_media.nsfw_score` has existed since migration 0000 with no writer. An upload on no post is never reached by the freeze, and the sweeper deletes it after a day (C 17).
- **Nothing counts the recipients** (DSA Art. 24(3)), and nothing flags a wave of linked reports (M 147).

**What binds 3d.** korbat's promise is that every removal cites a public rule, shows the author what happened and can be put before a person, and that there is no silent reach reduction. An automated step is where that promise is easiest to break, so the owner's rulings (section 2) bound the model before it was written: a program acts at most temporarily and protectively, says so at once, and never has the last word; nobody at korbat opens a matched image; no public figure points at a person; every part that needs a third party is a mechanism behind an adapter that is off. The law that applies to a micro platform is met without the parts that do not bind it: the statement of automated means (DSA Art. 17(3)(c)), the terms' description of each tool (Art. 14(1)), the recipients' figure that Art. 24(3) obliges korbat to give on request, the yearly report of TCO Art. 7(2) in a year with an order. The Art. 15 report, the publication of Art. 24(2) and the Transparency Database do not bind a micro or small enterprise (Art. 15(2), 19(1); GT X3.3): the first and the last are not built (rows 4 and 6), and the recipients' figure is published by choice (row 8).

**This design delivers**, with every adapter off:

1. the quarantine: sealed files out of the store and out of the API's and the worker's reach, moved by a one-shot service that has no network and no database;
2. the release: a one-way end of a seal for good on a recorded leave or instruction to destroy, never on an authority's assessment alone, with its proof of destruction and its replay after a restore;
3. an outbox row for every image that stops being public, drained to an edge adapter, and cache headers that bound a copy without it;
4. the public pages `/rules` and `/transparency`, with yearly banded counts, the recipients' figure and the audit head's daily value;
5. the automated decision: a decision without a person that is always interim, holds one protective measure, is tied at commit to the system's audit row and its signal, is capped, is stated at once, and is open to "Ask for a person";
6. the mechanisms of two automated tools, each reachable only through its test adapter until the owner acts: the scorer for rule R1 and the matcher against known material for rule R2, with the hold of an upload on no post that the source reports as an exact match of what it classifies as child sexual abuse material, and a flag for a person for every other match;
7. the flag "possible coordinated reporting", shown to staff and read by nothing else.

After 3d, sub-project 3 is complete. The going-public gate (C 17) is met by Tasks 1 and 2 of this design together with 3f's order path and the owner's list (section 17).

**Short names**, used in every section: C, E and F are the 3c, 3e and 3f designs (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-02-moderation-cases-3c-design.md`, `2026-10-09-account-sanctions-3e-design.md`, `2026-10-09-authorities-orders-3f-design.md`), each with its section; M is the main design, by line. GT, GA and GK are the gap research `korbat-scratch/research-3d/gap-X-transparency.md`, `gap-X-automation.md` and `gap-X-known-material.md`; IN is `inputs.md` there (scope items D1 to D28, disagreements P3-1 to P3-24, gaps X1 to X18); LAB is `lab-3d/` there, with its runs A, C, D and E (section 3). "Row N" is row N of section 2. "The system" is the system actor, `SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID` (`apps/api/src/auth/admin.ts:7`), which has no profile and no key.

## 2. Decisions taken without the user

The owner asked for 3d to be designed without them and ruled seven points before the model was written; the model's architect decided the rest, and the orchestrator ruled the model's six open points. This section records all of it. The mechanics are stated once, in the section each row names; a row gives the decision, the alternative and its cost, and what it rests on.

**One list, not three.** Section 17 is the list the owner works through and the README prints: it holds every line of the two lists below with its steps. The two lists here are its index by row. A row that the table flags `(owner)` or `(counsel)` and that has no line in section 17 is a fault of this design, since a line that is missing there is a thing nobody does.

**For the owner**, before anything is switched on:

- *Who answers an objection to the processing* (GDPR Art. 21), which the terms offer at the contact address (rows 8 and 33).

**The owner's rulings** (2026-10-09), cited in the table as "ruling N":

1. Mechanisms now, providers by the owner: every part that needs a third party or a fetched artefact is behind an adapter that is off by default and has a test adapter. The Transparency Database is not fed.
2. No dependency is added by a model, and none that needs an install script or native code without the reason stated; korbat's own small implementation where no package qualifies.
3. Nobody at korbat opens an image reported or matched as child sexual abuse material. No text says more of a match or a score than is known.
4. An automated step never has the last word: at most temporary and protective, stated at once with the sentence on automated means, with a simple way to a person from the first minute; the fallback "only raise an urgent item" is a setting.
5. The public pages point at no person; an order under a non-disclosure decision is never countable from outside while its hold runs.
6. The release is a one-way end recorded with the authority's reference; its periods are constants, and the destructive step waits for a recorded authority's answer and an admin's confirmed action.
7. 3d changes no migration of 3c, 3e or 3f.

**The orchestrator's rulings on the model's open points**, cited as O1 to O6:

- **O3.** 3f's target of 55 minutes stays (row 13), with a dated note in F 16.
- **O4.** A task that replaces a function begins by running the lab again on the built code. The lab's scripts were written against migrations 0016 and 0017 and cannot run against the built code as they are, so "again" means: each case the lab accepted and each refusal it measured becomes a test on the built code, with the same code (section 6, "Replacing a function").
- **O5.** A held upload is a record of its own, not a case (row 35).
- **O6.** The three defaults stand: `AUTOMATION_R1_ACTS=off`, `AUTOMATION_R2_ACTS=on`, `RECIPIENTS_SIGNED_OUT=on`. Each is flagged for the owner, and no tool runs, and none takes a measure, before the owner has set the date of row 49 that covers it.

**The review round's rulings** (2026-10-09, `korbat-scratch/research-3d/review-3d-rulings.md`), cited as "review ruling N" under that file's numbers. The first six are invariants that sections 6, 7 and 11 hold:

1. **Destruction needs leave, not an assessment.** An authority's recorded answer `illegal` is an assessment: by itself it changes nothing about the files, which stay sealed and in the quarantine. Sealed files are destroyed only on a recorded leave or instruction to destroy, from the authority or a court, with its reference, recorded from the command line as a fact of its own, and on an admin's confirmed action. `not_illegal` supports the unsealing; no answer supports nothing. The terms promise no destruction and no period. The author is not mailed an authority's assessment (rows 41, 44 and 46).
2. **An image found by a match is never opened by staff, whatever the answer.** The one function that serves staff an image refuses an image that an unerased match record names, on every case, also after an admin has answered without a seal (rows 26 and 27).
3. **Only what the source classifies as child sexual abuse material acts.** A match of any other class refuses nothing, holds nothing, seals and freezes nothing and cites no rule: it is recorded and shown to a person as a flag (row 28).
4. **Only what the source calls an exact match acts by itself.** A `near` match, or any answer short of exact, is a flag for a person (rows 27 and 28).
5. **A held or refused upload is in no reader and no export** (row 35).
6. **What a refused upload leaves behind agrees with what the person is told** (rows 35 and 37).
7. The console instructs nothing about reporting: the two ends of a hold are worded neutrally, none is preselected, and what counsel advises is in the runbook (row 35).
8. A handled match is marked on the match record itself, so nothing the retention job deletes makes the sweep act twice (6.7, 6.8).
9. The quarantine's receipt is taken line by line; one bad line never stops a run, and no file is left in the quarantine without a record (6.1, row 38).

Rulings 10 to 12 are about the wiring, the tasks and the names, and are applied in sections 5, 10, 12 and 13.

**The table.** Flags: `(owner)` the owner may overturn; `(counsel)` rests on a reading of law that counsel must confirm. A row without a flag follows from a ruling, from the three designs or from a measurement. Every number is a constant of one SQL function (`automation_rules()`, `release_rules()`, `transparency_rules()`, section 6) mirrored in the contracts. "Cautious" means: among the choices a source supports, the one that never exposes, never destroys and never tells more than is known.

"The same fingerprint" is said of a cryptographic hash alone; of a perceptual hash, whatever the source called the match, the words are "a similar fingerprint, which can also happen to different images", so the statement carries the hash type and not only the kind of match. No text says the image "is" such material, that korbat "confirmed" it, that the account "posted" such material, that nobody has seen the image, or that a person looked at it where no view is on record (row 26). A flag (row 28) is worded for staff alone: the source, its class and the kind of match. A score's sentence says that a program rated the image as likely within rule R1. The source is named only once it has allowed that. `(owner)` `(counsel)` for naming the source | | Ruling 3; review rulings 3 and 4; GK X7.5, X18.4 |
| 37 | The match record | `media_matches`: the image id, the case when there is one, the source, its list version, the hash type, the kind of match, the classification as returned, the hash value, the time, and the time the program was done with it (review ruling 8). No account column, no text. Staff see it on the case; the author sees the source's name in the statement. Erased 180 days after its case closed, its post was released, or its upload's hold ended without a report or was released, unless a seal for good on a post that is not released or a held upload still rests on it; a record that has neither a case nor a refusal, which is a flagged upload that was never posted, 180 days after it was made. Erasing sets the hash and the classification null and takes the account and the objection from the record's refusal: what stays says that an upload was refused on a day, by which source and kind of match, and how its hold ended, and it names nobody (review ruling 6). The count "other refused uploads of the same uploader" that an admin is shown never counts a hold that ended without a report, so a mistake of the source does not weigh on the next decision. `(counsel)` for the period and for GDPR Art. 10 | On the account: a marker that outlives a mistake (GK X7.5). | GK X11.5, X7.5 |

A seal taken while deciding, a person's or the program's, leaves its files in the store: it is meant to end within hours either way. `(owner)` | Every seal, moved by the worker on a request file: the decoder of untrusted images would mount the quarantine, and bringing files back would be an API's request. A service with a database role: a new role and network for a job that runs a few times a year. | C 17; F 7.14; IN X12 |

The price is stated: a lost disk loses the sealed files, and an image that an unsealing was to return is then recorded as lost and its author is told so (row 38). The API's image creates the mount path with that owner and mode, so a new volume takes them (section 5). `(owner)` `(counsel)` | A second encrypted copy off the server: more copies of material korbat may hold only for its duty (GK X13.3). | GK X13.5 |
